div.p: Make a white sauce with flour, butter, salt and milk. Beat yolks of eggs; add sugar and white sauce. Cut and fold in the well-beaten whites. Bake in individual ramekin dishes in a moderate oven, twenty to thirty minutes. Serve immediately with Orange or Sherry Sauce.

div.head: Orange Soufflé

list.item:
3 egg yolks
3 egg whites
3 tablespoons powdered sugar
rind of one half orange
1 tablespoon orange juice
½ tablespoon lemon juice
¼ teaspoon salt

div.p: Beat yolks until lemon-colored and thick. Add sugar, fruit juice and rind. Carefully fold in beaten whites. Pour into buttered dish, and bake fifteen to twenty minutes in moderate oven. Serve with Strawberry Sauce.

div.head: Bread Pudding

list.item:
2 cups bread crumbs
4 cups milk
3 eggs
½ cup sugar
1 teaspoon salt
2 tablespoons butter
cinnamon and nutmeg

div.p: Soak bread in milk; add beaten eggs and remaining ingredients. Bake one hour. Serve with hard sauce.

div.head: Bread Queen
div.p: Use rule for Bread Pudding, using whites of four eggs for meringue, and the yolks in the pudding instead of the three eggs. Before spreading on meringue, cover pudding with a layer of jam. Brown meringue slightly in the oven, and serve pudding hot or cold with cream.

div.head: Cracker Queen
div.p: Substitute one and one half cups cracker crumbs for bread crumbs in Bread Pudding, and add one cup seeded raisins cut in small pieces. Bake the same as Bread Pudding.

div.head: Buttered Bread Pudding
div.p: Butter twelve slices of bread; arrange in baking dish. Cover with four cups milk, four slightly beaten eggs, three fourths cup sugar, one half teaspoon salt, and the grated rind and juice of one lemon. Bake one and one half hours in slow oven. Serve with Hard Sauce.

div.head: Cocoanut Pudding
div.p: Use rule for Buttered Bread Pudding, sprinkle each bread layer with shredded cocoanut and chopped and seeded raisins. Serve with hard sauce.

div.head: Steamed Blueberry Dumpling

list.item:
4 cups blueberries
2 cups sugar
1 teaspoon vinegar
1 tablespoon butter
2 cups flour
4 teaspoons baking powder
1 teaspoon salt
¾ cup milk

div.p: Mix flour, baking powder and salt; add butter, mix until mealy; add milk. Put sugar, berries and vinegar in bottom of buttered baking dish. Cover with flour mixture and steam forty-five minutes. Serve in dish in which it is cooked.

div.head: Raspberry Dumpling
div.p: Prepare in the same way as Steamed Blueberry Dumpling, using four cups of raspberries instead of blueberries.

div.head: Blackberry Dumpling
div.p: Substitute blackberries for blueberries, and proceed as for Steamed Blueberry Dumpling.

div.head: Cherry Duff
div.p: Substitute two quarts cherries, in rule for making Blueberry Dumpling.

div.head: Peach Duff
div.p: Use rule for Blueberry Dumpling, substituting one quart peaches for blueberries.

div.head: Fruit Snowballs
div.p: Use receipt for making Snow Puffs. When done, sprinkle with powdered sugar and garnish with Cherry Sauce.

div.head: Steamed Rice Pudding

list.item:
1 cup rice
1½ teaspoons salt
8 cups cold water

div.p: Cook in steamer until water is absorbed and each kernel is separated. The time depends upon the age of the rice.

div.head: Caramel Rice Pudding

list.item:
1 cup rice
6 cups milk
1 teaspoon salt
2 eggs
1 cup sugar
grated rind of one half orange

div.p: Cook rice in milk, in double boiler, two hours; then add salt, eggs slightly beaten, and orange rind. Caramelize the sugar. When a golden brown liquid, pour into a hot pudding mold, coating the whole inner surface. Add rice mixture, cover and cook in oven in a pan of water twenty minutes. Remove from oven, let stand five minutes, turn on serving dish, and serve with Soft Custard.

div.head: Snow Puffs

list.item:
½ cup butter
1 cup sugar
½ cup milk
2½ cups flour
3 teaspoons baking powder
4 egg whites
½ teaspoon salt

div.p: Cream butter; add sugar, flour, baking powder and salt alternately with milk. Beat well; add the stiffly beaten whites; steam forty-five minutes in buttered popover cups. Serve with Strawberry Sauce.

div.head: Blueberry Puffs
div.p: Use rule for Snow Puffs and serve surrounded by a sauce made by cooking two cups blueberries and one cup sugar together twenty minutes.

div.head: Cottage Pudding

list.item:
1 cup sugar
¼ cup butter
2 eggs
1 cup milk
2 cups flour
3 teaspoons baking powder
¼ teaspoon salt

div.p: Cream butter and sugar together; add yolks of eggs beaten until thick, flour in which baking powder and salt have been sifted, alternately with milk; beat well and add the well-beaten whites. Pour into a well-buttered pudding dish. Bake forty-five minutes. Serve with Lemon, Vanilla, or Wine Sauce.

div.head: Steamed Cottage Pudding
div.p: Prepare the same as Cottage Pudding. Pour into buttered mold; steam one and one half hours. Serve with Lemon or Strawberry Sauce.

div.head: Indian Pudding, Steamed

list.item:
1 cup corn meal
⅓ cup sour milk
½ cup molasses
⅓ cup chopped suet
1 teaspoon salt
1 teaspoon soda
few grains ginger

div.p: Mix soda with sour milk, add other ingredients, pour into buttered mold, and steam four hours. Serve with Molasses Sauce.

div.head: Baked Indian Pudding

list.item:
6 cups milk
¼ cup corn meal
¼ cup molasses
1 tablespoon butter
½ teaspoon salt
few grains ginger

div.p: Scald one pint of milk with corn meal and cook twenty minutes; add remaining milk and rest of ingredients. Pour into deep earthen dish and bake, set in a pan of hot water, in a slow oven, four hours. The afternoon fire is the one best suited for cooking this pudding.

div.head: Indian Rice Pudding

list.item:
4 cups milk
¼ cup rice
½ cup molasses
2 tablespoons butter
½ teaspoon ginger
¼ teaspoon salt

div.p: Mix ingredients in the order given, pour into deep baking dish, set in a pan of hot water, and bake two hours. Stir once during cooking.

div.head: Indian Rice with Apples
div.p: To Indian Rice Pudding, add two cups pared and quartered apples.

div.head: Indian Tapioca Pudding

list.item:
½ cup pearl tapioca
6 cups scalded milk
¼ cup Indian meal
1 cup molasses
¼ cup butter
2 teaspoons salt
2 cups cold milk

div.p: Soak tapioca in cold water over night. Cook Indian meal and scalded milk in double boiler twenty minutes; add tapioca, molasses, butter, salt. Pour into buttered baking dish; cook two hours in slow oven.
At the end of the first hour, add the cold milk. Serve hot with butter or cream.

div.head: Rice Pudding

list.item:
½ cup rice
1 teaspoon salt
½ teaspoon nutmeg
4 tablespoons sugar
½ cup seeded raisins
4 cups hot milk
2 cups cold milk

div.p: Mix first six ingredients; pour into buttered pudding dish; cook in a slow oven two hours, stirring occasionally the first hour. At the end of two hours add the cold milk and cook half an hour longer.
Serve with sugar and cream.

div.head: Christmas Plum Pudding

list.item:
2 cups soft bread crumbs
2 cups chopped suet
1 cup chopped raisins
1 cup chopped citron
1 cup cleaned currants
1 teaspoon salt
1 teaspoon nutmeg
6 eggs
½ cup brandy
½ tablespoon lemon rind

div.p: Mix ingredients; pour into buttered mold; cover and steam four hours; bake in oven one half hour. Serve with Wine Sauce.

div.head: Graham Plum Pudding

list.item:
1½ cups graham flour
1 cup molasses
½ cup milk
1 cup seeded raisins
1 teaspoon cinnamon
½ teaspoon cloves
1 egg
½ teaspoon soda
2 tablespoons butter

div.p: Beat egg; add liquids, flour in which soda has been sifted, fruit, spices and melted butter. Pour into buttered baking powder tins and steam four hours. Serve with Brown Sugar Sauce.

div.head: Steamed Fig Pudding

list.item:
1 cup chopped figs
½ cup chopped suet
3 eggs
2¼ cups soft bread crumbs
⅓ cup milk
1 cup brown sugar
1 teaspoon salt

div.p: Cover bread crumbs with milk. Chop figs and suet together, add other ingredients, pour in buttered melon mold and steam from three and one half to four hours. Serve with Stirling Sauce.

div.head: Date Pudding
div.p: Use rule for Fig Pudding, adding one cup each chopped dates and shredded almonds, and omit figs.

div.head: Roly Poly Pudding
div.p: Roll pastry or a baking-powder biscuit dough very thin, about one eighth of an inch in thickness, spread with jam, blackberry, black currant, or raspberry. Roll like a jelly roll, press, and close the ends as tight as possible. Tie in a floured cloth, and cook in boiling water two hours, or steam in steamer one hour. Remove from cloth and serve on hot platter with Foamy Sauce.

div.head: Cream Croquettes

list.item:
2 cups milk scalded
4 tablespoons cornstarch
¼ cup cold milk
¾ cup sugar
2 eggs
½ cup chopped almonds
1 teaspoon vanilla

div.p: Mix cornstarch and cold milk, add hot milk, and cook in double boiler until mixture thickens. Add eggs well beaten, sugar, almonds and vanilla. Cook two minutes. Pour into shallow pan; chill; cut into squares or rounds; dip in crumbs, egg and crumbs, fry in hot fat. Drain on brown paper, roll in powdered sugar, and serve. Serve with Lemon Sauce.

div.head: English Pudding

list.item:
½ cup butter
1 cup seeded raisins
1 cup molasses
¾ cup milk
1 teaspoon salt
1 teaspoon soda
½ teaspoon cloves
½ teaspoon cinnamon
½ teaspoon mace
3-¾ cups flour

div.p: Cream butter; add remaining ingredients; pour into buttered mold; steam four hours. Serve with Brandy Sauce or Foamy Sauce.

div.head: Apricot Sauce

list.item:
½ cup apricot jam, or
1 cup apricot juice
½ cup sugar
½ cup water
1 teaspoon cornstarch
1 tablespoon lemon juice
few grains salt

div.p: Boil all ingredients ten minutes.

div.head: Apple Sauce

list.item:
1 cup chopped apple
1 tablespoon arrowroot
few grains salt
½ cup cold water
few grains cinnamon
1 tablespoon lemon juice
grated rind of ½ lemon

div.p: Cook all together ten minutes. Strain, add more lemon juice if needed.

div.head: Banana Sauce

list.item:
1 cup water
½ cup sugar
3 banana pulps
3 tablespoons lemon juice
2 eggs
few grains salt

div.p: Boil sugar and water ten minutes. Mix remaining ingredients and pour hot sirup on to them. Beat well and serve hot.

div.head: Creamy Sauce

list.item:
⅓ cup butter
⅓ cup powdered sugar
2 tablespoons cream
2 tablespoons wine

div.p: Mix butter and sugar until creamy, add wine and cream. Cook over hot water until liquefied.

div.head: Cream Sauce

list.item:
1 cup powdered sugar
1 egg
2 cups cream
1 teaspoon vanilla

div.p: Mix egg yolk and sugar; add white of egg beaten until stiff, flavoring, and just before sending to the table the beaten cream. Serve cold.

div.head: Cream Brandy Sauce

list.item:
1 cup water
1 cup sugar
⅓ cup cream
3 egg yolks
2 tablespoons brandy
few orange rind gratings
few grains salt

div.p: Cook sugar and water ten minutes; beat yolks; add cream, brandy, salt, orange rind gratings. Add sugar and water slowly and beat until mixture thickens.

div.head: Cream Sherry Sauce

list.item:
3 tablespoons butter
⅓ cup sugar
2 egg yolks
⅔ cup cream
3 tablespoons sherry
few grains salt

div.p: Mix butter, sugar, yolks and cream; cook in double boiler until mixture thickens; add wine, and serve.

div.head: Caramel Sauce

list.item:
1 cup sugar
1 cup boiling water

div.p: Caramelize sugar in clean saucepan. When a light brown color, add water, and simmer fifteen minutes.

div.head: Cherry Sauce

list.item:
1½ cups cherries
1 cup claret
½ cup sugar
½ glass Currant Jelly
juice and rind of ½ lemon
1 inch stick cinnamon

div.p: Remove stones from cherries and cook all ingredients together until sirupy. Strain and serve.

div.head: Claret Sauce

list.item:
1 cup sugar
1 cup water
1 cup claret

div.p: Boil sugar and water until sirupy, add claret, and serve hot or cold.

div.head: Coffee Sauce

list.item:
½ cup sugar
2 eggs
¾ cup black coffee
½ cup cream
few grains salt

div.p: Mix eggs, sugar, salt, and coffee, and cook in double boiler until mixture thickens. Chill; add beaten cream and serve cold.

div.head: Currant Sauce

list.item:
1 cup sugar
⅓ cup water
1 cup currant juice
2 tablespoons lemon juice

div.p: Boil sugar and water until sirupy; add currant juice and lemon juice. Serve hot or cold.

div.head: Currant Jelly Sauce

list.item:
1 cup sugar
¼ cup water
1 inch piece stick cinnamon
½ cup currant jelly

div.p: Boil sugar, water and cinnamon until sirupy. Remove cinnamon; add jelly; when melted, strain and serve.

div.head: Custard Sauce

list.item:
2 cups milk
3 egg yolks
1 teaspoon butter
⅓ cup sugar
2 egg whites
1 teaspoon vanilla
few grains salt

div.p: Make a custard of milk, egg yolks, sugar and salt; when thick, add butter, flavoring and beaten whites. Serve cold.

div.head: Foamy Sauce No. 1

list.item:
1 cup sugar
3 egg whites
1 cup milk
rind and juice of 1 lemon

div.p: Heat the milk. Beat egg whites until stiff; add sugar, continue beating; add milk and flavoring, continue beating. Serve when foamy.

div.head: Foamy Sauce No. 2

list.item:
½ cup butter
1 cup powdered sugar
1 egg yolk
2 tablespoons wine
2 egg whites

div.p: Cream butter; add sugar, yolk of egg and wine. Cook over hot water until hot. Remove from fire and add beaten whites of eggs.

div.head: Foamy Sauce No. 3

list.item:
3 egg whites
½ cup powdered sugar
rind of ½ lemon
1 cup boiling water
1 teaspoon flavoring

div.p: Beat whites until stiff; add sugar and flavoring and continue beating, adding hot water very gradually. Serve hot or cold.

div.head: Fruit Sauce No. 1

list.item:
1 cup sugar
1 cup water
½ cup fruit juice
2 tablespoons arrowroot

div.p: Mix arrowroot, sugar and water; boil ten minutes, stirring constantly. Add fruit juice and cook until sirupy, and serve hot.

div.head: Fruit Sauce No. 2

list.item:
1 cup sugar
½ cup water
1 cup pulp and juice of fruit
1 tablespoon lemon juice

div.p: Boil sugar and water until sirupy. Add lemon and fruit juice and pulp. Serve hot without straining.

div.head: Grape Sauce

list.item:
1 cup sugar
⅓ cup water
1 cup grape juice
1 tablespoon orange or lemon juice

div.p: Boil all together until sirupy. Serve hot or cold.

div.head: Hard Sauce No. 1

list.item:
½ cup butter
1 cup powdered sugar
wine, brandy, or vanilla
1 teaspoon hot water

div.p: Cream butter; add sugar by the teaspoon, and beat until light and creamy. Flavor and serve.

div.head: Hard Sauce No. 2

list.item:
½ cup butter
1 cup powdered sugar
1 teaspoon vanilla
1 tablespoon brandy
¼ cup beaten cream

div.p: Cream butter; add sugar and cream alternately, flavoring, and serve very cold.

div.head: Stirling Sauce

list.item:
½ cup butter
1 cup powdered sugar
3 tablespoons milk
2 tablespoons wine

div.p: Mix sugar, wine and milk, and warm in double boiler or over hot water. Add to creamed butter slowly. Do not permit the sugar mixture to become hot, only warm.

div.head: Kirsch Sauce
div.p: Use rule for Stirling Sauce, substituting one fourth cup kirsch for wine.

div.head: Lemon Sauce

list.item:
2 teaspoons arrowroot or cornstarch
2 cups water
1 cup sugar
grated rind and juice one lemon
1½ tablespoons butter

div.p: Mix arrowroot or cornstarch with sugar. Add boiling water and cook twenty minutes. Add flavoring and butter. Serve hot.

div.head: Maple Sauce

list.item:
2 egg yolks
½ cup maple sirup
½ cup beaten cream
few grains salt

div.p: Beat yolks until thick; add maple sirup and cook until it thickens. Add beaten cream, salt. Chill and serve.

div.head: Maraschino Sauce

list.item:
1 cup sugar
1 tablespoon arrowroot
2 cups boiling water
2 tablespoons maraschino

div.p: Mix sugar, arrowroot and boiling water; boil ten minutes. Add maraschino. Chill and serve.

div.head: Orange Sauce No. 1

list.item:
grated rind, juice and pulp of 3 oranges
⅓ cup powdered sugar
3 egg whites
1 tablespoon lemon juice

div.p: Beat whites until stiff; add remaining ingredients. Serve cold.

div.head: Orange Sauce No. 2
div.p: Make the same as Lemon Sauce, substituting the juice and rind of two oranges for lemon.

div.head: Rum Sauce

list.item:
½ cup powdered sugar
2 egg yolks
2 egg whites
3 tablespoons rum
½ cup beaten cream

div.p: Mix sugar, yolks of eggs and rum, then the stiffly beaten whites. Cook until thick; add the beaten cream. Chill and serve.

div.head: Sabayon Sauce No. 1

list.item:
4 egg yolks
¼ cup wine
4 tablespoons powdered sugar
1 tablespoon lemon juice

div.p: Mix all ingredients and, just before serving, cook over hot water until it begins to thicken.

div.head: Sabayon Sauce No. 2

list.item:
1 whole egg
2 egg yolks
½ cup sugar
½ cup sherry
1 tablespoon lemon juice

div.p: Mix all ingredients and cook over hot water, stirring constantly until mixture thickens.

div.head: Strawberry Sauce

list.item:
½ cup butter
1 cup powdered sugar
1 cup strawberries
1 beaten egg white

div.p: Cream butter; add sugar, egg white; beat well; add strawberries crushed to a pulp. Serve.

div.head: Vanilla Sauce

list.item:
½ cup butter
1 cup powdered sugar
1 cup cream
1 tablespoon vanilla

div.p: Cream butter; add sugar, beaten cream and flavoring. Heat over hot water until all is liquid. Serve hot.

div.head: Brown Sugar Sauce

list.item:
⅓ cup butter
1 cup brown sugar
2 teaspoons vanilla
⅓ cup cream

div.p: Mix cream and brown sugar, and add to creamed butter very gradually. When of creamy consistency, add flavoring.

div.head: Italian Sauce

list.item:
2 tablespoons butter
¾ cup powdered sugar
2 teaspoons cornstarch
½ cup candied cherries
3 egg yolks
juice and rind of 1 lemon
½ cup boiling water
½ cup angelica cut in pieces

div.p: Cream butter; add sugar and cornstarch, yolks of eggs well beaten, and boiling water; boil three minutes; add remaining ingredients and serve.

div.head: Chocolate Sauce

list.item:
2 ounces Lowney’s Premium Chocolate
1 cup sugar
½ cup water
2 tablespoons butter
¼ teaspoon salt
1 teaspoon vanilla

div.p: Cook all the ingredients except vanilla twelve minutes; add vanilla, and serve hot. This sauce is especially good served with Vanilla Ice Cream, but is good with any gelatine dessert.

div.head: Orange Chocolate Sauce

list.item:
4 tablespoons Lowney’s Premium Chocolate grated
3 tablespoons butter
3 egg yolks
4 tablespoons sugar
¼ cup rich milk
⅓ cup orange juice
grated rind of 1 orange

div.p: Melt chocolate in top of double boiler; add butter, stir until well mixed; add egg yolks, one at a time, sugar, and milk. Cook until thickened, add orange juice and rind, and serve at once.

div.head: Chocolate Cream Sauce

list.item:
¾ cup powdered sugar
1 cup cream
¼ cup Lowney’s Premium Chocolate grated
⅛ teaspoon salt
4 tablespoons hot water
1 egg white
1 teaspoon almond extract, or
1 tablespoon cordial

div.p: Melt chocolate; add sugar and boiling water; cook until glossy. Cool. Beat cream until stiff; add chocolate mixture gradually; cut and fold in beaten white. Flavor and serve. One half cup Lowney’s Cocoa may be substituted for the chocolate.

div.head: Rule for lining Plate and making Cover for Pie with Two Crusts
div.p: Roll the paste one quarter inch thick. Cut paste an eighth of an inch larger than plate. Cut strips three quarters inch wide for a rim. Cut upper crust at least one eighth inch larger than plate. Arrange lower crust on plate, wet edges with cold water, lay strips of paste or rim on this, taking care to lap and seal the ends with cold water. Fill the pie with whatever material is to be used. Cut little slits in center of upper crust. Lay on pie; wet edges of rim. Have all edges even, leaving fullness in center to allow for shrinking. Press edges lightly but firmly.

div.head: Rule for making a Pie with Under Crust only
div.p: Roll paste one eighth inch thick. Cut one inch larger than plate. Spread on plate; fold edge under, making paste the size of plate. This edge may be fluted or plain. Chill before filling.

div.head: Rule for Baking Pies
div.p: Perforated tin pie plates secure a well-baked under crust. Place pie in hot oven at first, reducing heat after crust becomes hardened. Turn frequently while baking, and bake until a golden brown—about forty-five minutes.

div.head: Chopped Paste

list.item:
1½ cups flour
4 tablespoons lard
4 tablespoons butter
½ teaspoon salt
cold water

div.p: Sift salt and flour; add lard and butter when thoroughly chilled. Chop until like meal; add cold water to make a stiff dough. Chill; roll on a floured cloth or molding board into a rectangular shape; fold ends towards center, double, turn halfway round, and roll again.
This paste is a superior one. Chill before rolling for pies.

div.head: Plain Paste
div.p: Use same rule as for Chopped Paste. Chop lard into sifted flour; when thoroughly mixed, add salt and water to form dough. Chill; roll in rectangular piece; place butter which has previously been shaped, flattened, and chilled on middle of one side of paste; fold over other side, press edges together, and fold one end under and one end over butter, making six layers. Roll again into rectangle; fold in same way, and so continue three times. If butter begins to soften, roll paste in cheese cloth and place on ice until hard enough to roll easily. Be careful not to wet the cheese cloth.

div.head: Puff Paste

list.item:
1 pound butter
1 pound flour
cold water

div.p: Shape and flatten butter into a round cake. Chill. Sift flour several times; add cold water to form a dough a little stiffer than for baking powder biscuit. Chill. Place butter in same way as directed in Plain Paste and roll paste seven times. Chill if necessary between each rolling.

div.head: Apple Pie No. 1
div.p: Use either Puff or Plain Paste. For filling for a medium-sized pie tin, use three cups pared and sliced apples, one half cup sugar, one eighth teaspoon salt, one tablespoon butter, one fourth teaspoon cinnamon, one tablespoon lemon juice, and grated rind of one half lemon.

div.head: Apple Pie No. 2
div.p: Use either Puff or Plain Paste. For filling use rule for Apple Sauce, and season to taste.

div.head: Blueberry Pie
div.p: Line a deep perforated tin with Plain or Chopped Paste; brush with water or white of egg. Fill with floured blueberries; add sugar, butter, salt and vinegar. Allow one cup of sugar to three cups of berries, one tablespoon butter, one eighth teaspoon salt, and one half teaspoon vinegar. Cover with crust and bake.

div.head: Blackberry Pie
div.p: Use rule for Blueberry Pie, omitting flour and vinegar.

div.head: Cranberry Pie
div.p: Use Plain or Chopped Paste. Fill with two cups cranberries, one and one half cups sugar, one quarter cup water, and one tablespoon butter. Cover with upper crust or a lattice of paste strips; or bake without any upper crust. Decorate when done with pastry baked in fancy shapes.

div.head: Cranberry Pie No. 2
div.p: Use Plain Paste. For filling, mix one and one quarter cups chopped cranberries, one half cup chopped raisins, one cup sugar, one quarter cup water, and one tablespoon butter.
This is sometimes called Mock Cherry Pie.

div.head: Currant Pie
div.p: Use Plain Paste. For filling, mix two cups cleaned, fresh currants, two cups sugar, two tablespoons flour, two eggs, and one eighth teaspoon salt.
Bake with two crusts; or omit upper crust and cover with meringue when cooked.

div.head: Custard Pie
div.p: Use Plain or Chopped Paste. For filling, mix three eggs, one fourth cup sugar, one eighth teaspoon salt, one eighth teaspoon nutmeg, and two cups milk. Bake in slow oven.

div.head: Citron Pie
div.p: Use Plain or Chopped Paste. For filling, mix two cups seeded raisins chopped, two cups citron chopped, one and one half cups sugar, grated rind of one lemon, four tablespoons lemon juice, one eighth teaspoon salt.

div.head: Cocoanut Pie
div.p: Line a plate with Plain Paste; fill with following mixture: two cups milk, three egg yolks, one half cup sugar, two tablespoons cornstarch, one cup grated cocoanut, one fourth teaspoon salt, grated rind and juice of one lemon, and one tablespoon butter.

div.head: Date Pie
div.p: Use Plain Paste. Add one and one half cups of dates, which have been cooked in boiling water until tender and pressed through a sieve, to Custard Pie filling.

div.head: Lemon Pie No. 1
div.p: Use Plain Paste. For filling, mix two tablespoons cornstarch, one cup sugar, and one half cup boiling water, boil five minutes, add one tablespoon butter, juice and rind of one lemon, and two eggs well beaten.

div.head: Lemon Pie No. 2
div.p: Use Plain Paste. For filling, mix one cup sugar, yolks of four eggs, one eighth teaspoon salt, one cup milk, grated rind and juice of one lemon, and the whites of four eggs beaten until stiff. Cover with meringue when done.

div.head: Mince Pie
div.p: Use Plain Paste for under crust, fill with mince-meat, cover with Puff Paste.

div.head: Peach Pie
div.p: Use Plain or Chopped Paste. For filling use two cups peaches, cut into eighths, one cup sugar, one tablespoon butter, one eighth teaspoon salt, and two tablespoons water.

div.head: Plum Pie
div.p: Use Plain or Chopped Paste. Remove stones from two cups plums; add one half cup sugar; dredge with flour; add two tablespoons lemon juice and one tablespoon butter.

div.head: Prune Pie
div.p: Substitute prunes for plums and follow rule for Plum Pie.

div.head: Pumpkin Pie
div.p: Line pie plate with Plain Paste. For filling, mix one and one half cups stewed and strained pumpkin, one and one half cups milk, one egg, three fourths cup brown sugar, one tablespoon butter, one half teaspoon each of salt and ginger, and one teaspoon cinnamon.

div.head: Chocolate Cream Pie

list.item:
2 squares Lowney’s Premium Chocolate or
½ cup of Lowney’s Cocoa
¼ cup cornstarch
2 cups milk
2 egg whites
½ cup sugar
3 egg yolks
¼ teaspoon salt
1 tablespoon vanilla

div.p: Melt two squares Lowney’s Chocolate or one half cup Lowney’s Cocoa, add sugar, cornstarch, egg yolks, salt and milk. Cook in double boiler till thick, stirring constantly; flavor with vanilla. Pour into a baked pie crust shell, cover with a meringue made by beating egg whites till stiff and adding two tablespoons sugar; brown in oven and serve cold. See colored illustration, Plate VIII, opposite p. 227.

div.head: Rhubarb Pie
div.p: Use Plain Paste. For filling, mix two cups rhubarb cut in inch pieces, one cup sugar, two tablespoons each of butter and flour, one egg, one eighth teaspoon salt, and one teaspoon lemon juice.

div.head: Squash Pie
div.p: Use Chopped Paste. For filling, mix one cup stewed and strained squash, one half cup sugar, one half teaspoon salt, two eggs, one half teaspoon cinnamon, one fourth teaspoon nutmeg, and one half cup milk.
A very good pie may be made by using one and one half cups of the squash left from dinner, sweetening and seasoning it without adding eggs.

div.head: Mince Pie Filling

list.item:
3 lbs. lean beef finely chopped
2 lbs. suet finely chopped
3 qts. apples finely chopped
3 lbs. raisins seeded and chopped
2 lbs. currants
3 lbs. citron cut in small pieces
½ cup candied orange peel chopped
½ cup candied lemon peel chopped
½ cup lemon juice
¼ cup orange juice
2 tablespoons salt
4 cups sugar
1 cup coffee
2 cups cider
1 teaspoon cloves
1 teaspoon allspice
2 teaspoons cinnamon
3 cups brandy
1 cup sherry
1 cup Currant Jelly

div.p: Mix all ingredients except brandy and sherry, and cook two hours; add liquor; let stand in crock for a week before using.

div.head: Vol-au-vent No. 1
div.p: Roll Puff Paste one half inch thick. Cut out in desired shape, wet edges, and place one inch rim on wet edge. Prick several times in center that paste may rise evenly. Chill. Cut cover the size of space inside the rim. Decorate top of cover with paste circles, crescents, or diamonds, always wetting under surface with cold water before arranging. Chill before baking.

div.head: Pâté Shells
div.p: Roll Puff Paste one third inch thick; shape with round cutter; cut rings from one half the rounds. Place rings on rounds, using cold water to hold them together. Chill until stiff before baking.

div.head: Bouchées
div.p: Roll Puff Paste one fourth inch thick. Cut with small round cutter; make impression on round with smaller round cutter. Chill until stiff before baking.

div.head: Tarts
div.p: Roll Puff Paste a little less than one fourth inch in thickness. Cut in rounds, squares, or diamonds; put on rim, wetting edges. Chill and bake.

div.head: Vol-au-vent No. 2
div.p: Cover the outside of a charlotte russe mold with Puff Paste, cut one fourth inch thick. Prick surface of paste, chill, and bake. Cut a cover for vol-au-vent to fit mold; prick, chill, and bake. Remove vol-au-vent from mold immediately after baking.

div.head: Rule for Baking Puff Paste
div.p: Always chill Puff Paste before baking. Place in very hot oven; protect upper surface of paste, if necessary, at first.
Pâtés should be baked in twenty-four minutes; after the first fifteen, decrease heat.
Vol-au-vent should bake forty-five minutes to one hour, and should be turned frequently. Remove soft inside portion as soon as taken from oven. Tarts and bouchées should be baked the same as pâtés.

div.head: Frangipane Tartlets
div.p: Cover fluted patty tins with Puff Paste. Make covers a little larger than patty tins. Bake in a hot oven. Fill with Frangipane Cream. Cover with meringue, and decorate with cherries, angelica, and blanched and browned almonds.

div.head: Frangipane Cream
div.p: Mix two tablespoons flour, one fourth cup powdered sugar, and one fourth cup cream until smooth. Cook ten minutes, stirring constantly; add four egg yolks, one tablespoon each of sherry, lemon juice, lemon rind, and chopped citron. Cook in double boiler until mixture thickens.

div.head: Almond Sticks
div.p: Roll Puff Paste one eighth inch thick. Brush with white of egg, sprinkle with shredded almonds and powdered sugar. Cut in strips one half inch wide and three inches long. Bake in a quick oven.

div.head: Cheese Straws
div.p: Roll Puff Paste—trimmings will do for this purpose—one eighth inch thick. Sprinkle with salt, cayenne pepper, and grated cheese. To keep these ingredients on the paste, pat and fold in three layers. Roll again, spread, fold, and roll as before. Cut in strips half inch wide and five inches long. Bake in a quick oven.

div.head: Banbury Tarts
div.p: Make tarts and fill with the following cooked mixture: mix for filling, one cup seeded and chopped raisins, one cup sugar, three tablespoons cracker crumbs, one egg, one tablespoon butter, one eighth teaspoon salt, juice and rind of one lemon.

div.head: Banbury Squares
div.p: Roll Chopped Paste one fourth inch thick; cut in three inch squares. Put one and one half teaspoons Banbury mixture on one side of square, wet edges, fold to make a triangle, prick, and bake.

div.head: Apple Tarts
div.p: Fill tarts with Apple Sauce to which has been added one tablespoon butter.

div.head: Cranberry Tarts
div.p: Fill tarts with cranberry filling used for Cranberry Pie.

div.head: Lemon Tarts
div.p: Fill tarts with Lemon Cream used for Lemon Pie, cooked in double boiler until thick.

div.head: Peach Tarts
div.p: Cook two cups peaches cut in eighths, one cup sugar, one tablespoon lemon juice, one tablespoon butter, and a few grains salt, until peaches are tender. Cool and fill tarts.

div.head: Pineapple Tarts
div.p: Cook one cup grated pineapple, one fourth cup sugar, two egg yolks, grated rind and juice of one lemon, and few grains of salt, until thick. Chill and fill tarts.

div.head: Gooseberry Tart
div.p: For this tart cover the outside of a round agate-ware baking dish with Chopped Paste. Chill, bake. For filling, mix four cups gooseberries, one cup sugar, few gratings lemon rind, few gratings nutmeg. Stew until gooseberries are tender; add two tablespoons butter. Use hot or cold in paste shell. Serve with cream or Soft Custard.

div.head: Lemon Crisps
div.p: Cut Puff Paste in strips four inches long, one inch wide, and one fourth inch in thickness. Chill and bake. Arrange in pairs with Lemon Filling between.

div.head: Orange Crisps
div.p: Prepare the same as Lemon Crisps, using Orange Filling.

div.head: Chantilly Tarts
div.p: Fill tarts with Strawberry Jam; serve with whipped cream.

div.head: Crisp à la Russe
div.p: Roll Puff Paste one eighth inch thick. Cut in strips two inches wide and four inches long. Spread one half with jam or jelly, fold over other half, press edges together, bake in hot oven. Brush with white of egg, sprinkle with almonds. Brown in oven.

div.head:
CHAPTER XIV
CAKE AND COOKIES; FROSTINGS AND FILLINGS
Suggestions for making and baking Cake
div.p: 1st. Get all materials needed together.
2d. Attend to fire, making sure, if it is a coal fire, that there is sufficient coal to last through the baking.
3d. Measure all ingredients with same cup, dry ones first.
4th. Mix and sift all dry ingredients except sugar; if soda is used, sift through a very fine sieve before sifting with other ingredients.

div.head: Mixing Butter Cakes
div.p: Cream Butter.—Cream butter, that is, beat it with a spoon until it is of a creamy consistency; then add sugar very gradually; when well blended, add yolks of eggs which have been beaten with a Dover egg beater until lemon-colored and thick.

When the ingredients are thoroughly incorporated, add sifted dry ingredients alternately with the milk. When all milk and flour have been used, beat well; then cut and fold in the stiffly beaten whites of eggs. Pour into buttered and papered pan, having mixture a little higher on the sides than in the middle.

Cutting and Folding.—Cut through and through the mixture with a knife or side of a wooden spoon, fold by turning the spoon completely over, thereby blending the materials without breaking the air bubbles. Never stir or beat after cutting and folding.

div.head: Mixing Sponge Cake
div.p: Beat yolks of eggs until lemon-colored and thick; add sugar and continue beating; add flour; when well blended, cut and fold in the stiffly beaten whites of eggs. Pour into buttered and papered pan; bake in a round pan with a tube in the center.

div.head: Baking Cake
div.p: For baking both sponge and butter cakes divide the time into quarters. The first quarter, the cake should rise; the second quarter, form a crust and begin to brown; third quarter, continue browning; and fourth quarter, finish browning and shrink from the pan. When baked, this may be determined by pressing crust with the finger; if a depression is left the cake is not done; if the cake springs back and leaves no depression, it is done. Take from oven, invert on a cake cooler, remove paper, turn right-side up and cool. When cold, frost.

div.head: Time for baking Cake
div.p: Thin cakes and individual cakes require from twelve to fifteen minutes to bake; loaf cakes from thirty to sixty minutes according to size.
If the cake rises unevenly, the mixture is too thick or the oven is too hot.
If the oven seems too hot, when the cake is ready for the oven, put the cake in the oven, but do not close the oven door for the first five or ten minutes of baking.

div.head: To grease Tins
div.p: Warm pans slightly; brush with melted lard, suet, or clarified butter; cover bottom of pan only with tissue paper, then grease the paper.

Lard or suet is less apt to brown than butter, but many object to their use; if so, clarify the butter, by melting butter, letting stand until salt has settled to the bottom, then pouring off the liquid butter.

div.head: Plain Chocolate Cake

list.item:
½ cup butter
1½ cups sugar
2 cups flour
3 teaspoons baking powder
4 ounces Lowney’s Premium Chocolate
5 tablespoons boiling water
¼ teaspoon salt
½ cup milk
1 teaspoon vanilla
4 eggs

div.p: Cream the butter; add the sugar very gradually, yolks of eggs well beaten, flour in which the baking powder and salt have been sifted, milk, and chocolate mixed with water. Beat well; add beaten whites, pour into buttered pans, and bake forty to fifty minutes in a moderate oven. This cake may be baked in small cakes by omitting one fourth cup flour.

div.head: Chocolate Cake No. 2

list.item:
4 ounces Lowney’s Premium Chocolate
1½ cups sugar
½ cup butter
½ cup milk
2 cups flour
3 eggs
2 teaspoons baking powder
¼ teaspoon salt
3 tablespoons boiling water

div.p: Melt chocolate, add boiling water, and cook over hot water until smooth. Cream butter; add sugar gradually; when of a creamy consistency, add chocolate mixture, yolks of eggs well beaten, flour in which salt and baking powder have been sifted, and milk. Beat well; cut and fold in well-beaten whites; add flavoring. Pour into buttered pans and bake in a moderate oven thirty or forty minutes. Frost with White or Chocolate Frosting.
This mixture may be used for layer cakes by omitting one fourth cup flour and baking in layer cake pans.

div.head: Chocolate Raisin Cake

list.item:
1 cup butter
1½ cups sugar
¾ cup milk
5 egg yolks
¼ teaspoon salt
2 tablespoons sherry or brandy
2 squares Lowney’s Premium Chocolate, grated
½ teaspoon cinnamon
2 cups seeded raisins
3½ cups flour
3 teaspoons baking powder
5 egg whites

div.p: Cream butter; add sugar gradually, grated chocolate, raisins, cinnamon, baking powder and salt sifted with flour, milk. Beat well; add flavoring and well-beaten whites of eggs. Bake in deep buttered pans, forty minutes. This amount will make two loaves. The wine or brandy may be omitted, in which case, use one cup of milk instead of three fourths cup.

div.head: Chocolate Pound Cake

list.item:
1 cup butter
1 cup sugar
5 egg yolks
5 egg whites
½ teaspoon salt
¼ cup Lowney’s Premium Chocolate, grated
2 cups flour
¼ cup brandy
1 cup citron cut in small pieces

div.p: Cream butter; add sugar gradually, yolks of eggs beaten until thick and lemon-colored, flour, citron, salt. Beat well; cut and fold in whites of eggs beaten until stiff. Pour into buttered pans and bake one hour in a moderate oven. This cake may be baked in a buttered dripping pan and when cold cut into fancy shapes and iced.

div.head: Devil’s Food

list.item:
¾ cup butter
2 cups sugar
4 eggs
1 cup milk
8 tablespoons chocolate
2¼ cups flour
1 teaspoon cinnamon
¼ teaspoon clove
4 teaspoons baking powder
⅛ teaspoon salt

div.p: Cream the butter, add the sugar, the chocolate melted, eggs well beaten, flour sifted with baking powder, salt and spices, and the milk. Beat well, and bake in angel cake pan. Frost with Chocolate or Marshmallow Frosting.

div.head: Cocoa Cake

list.item:
½ cup butter
1½ cups sugar
4 eggs
½ cup Lowney’s Cocoa
½ cup milk
1½ cups flour
2 teaspoons baking powder
¼ teaspoon salt
1 teaspoon vanilla

div.p: Mix in the order given and beat well for five minutes. Bake in buttered pan thirty to forty minutes in moderate oven.
Little squares of cake with white icing and a walnut half on top

WALNUT CHOCOLATE CAKE
Plate IX. For Receipt see page 262

div.head: Walnut Chocolate Cake

list.item:
¼ cup Lowney’s Always Ready Chocolate Powder
½ cup butter
1½ cups flour
½ cup milk
1 cup walnut meats
1 cup sugar
2 egg yolks
2½ teaspoons baking powder
2 tablespoons hot water
1 teaspoon vanilla
salt

div.p: Cream butter; add sugar, yolks of eggs well beaten and flour in which baking powder has been sifted, milk, and chocolate which has been moistened with hot water; beat well and add walnut meats. Bake in buttered jelly cake pans about twenty minutes.

Spread one cake with one half cup of Lowney’s Sweet Chocolate Powder moistened with one fourth cup boiling water and flavored with one teaspoon vanilla. Sprinkle with broken walnuts, cover with other cake, and ice with White Frosting. See colored illustration, Plate IX, opposite.
pile of cake pieces with white icing

CHOCOLATE SPONGE CAKE
Plate X. For Receipt see page 262

div.head: Chocolate Sponge Cake

list.item:
¼ cup Lowney’s Always Ready Chocolate Powder
yolks of 3 eggs
¼ cup sugar
whites of 3 eggs
2 tablespoons hot water
¼ teaspoon salt
¼ cup pastry flour
1 teaspoon vanilla

div.p: Beat yolks until lemon-colored and thick; add sugar and continue beating. Mix chocolate with water, add to sugar mixture; cut and fold in flour, salt and beaten whites. Flavor and bake in buttered pan in a moderate oven three quarters of an hour. See colored illustration, Plate X, opposite p. 262.
served in goblet with whipped cream and a cherry

COCOA PARFAIT
Plate XI. For Receipt see page 302

div.head: Chocolate Nut Cakes

list.item:
4 squares Lowney’s Premium Chocolate, grated
1½ cups sugar
3 teaspoons baking powder
1 cup nut meats broken in pieces
2¼ cups flour
½ cup milk
8 egg whites
1 teaspoon vanilla
salt
¾ cup butter

div.p: Cream butter; add sugar, flour in which baking powder has been sifted, and milk, and beat well; add whites of eggs beaten stiff and nut meats; then add chocolate and vanilla. Pour into buttered gem pans and bake in hot oven twenty-five minutes.
cocoa in beacutiful tea cup topped with whipped cream and a cherry spoon on the side

COCOA FRAPPÉ
Plate XII. For Receipt see page 295

div.head: Simple Butter Cake

list.item:
½ cup butter
2 cups sugar
4 egg yolks
1 cup milk
3 cups flour
4 teaspoons baking powder
4 egg whites
1 teaspoon flavoring
¼ teaspoon salt

div.p: Follow directions for making Butter Cake, and bake in a loaf in a moderate oven forty minutes, or in rounds twenty minutes.

div.head: Currant Cake
div.p: Add one cup currants to Simple Butter Cake. Bake in loaves or rounds.

div.head: Layer Cake
div.p: Bake Simple Butter Cake in four square shallow pans. Fill with Lemon Cream, Cocoanut Cream, Chocolate Cream, or Jelly.

div.head: Gold Cake

list.item:
¾ cup butter
1½ cups sugar
8 egg yolks
1 egg
2¼ cups flour
4 teaspoons baking powder
1½ cups milk
¼ teaspoon salt
1 teaspoon lemon extract, or
1 teaspoon orange extract

div.p: Follow directions for Butter Cake, and bake in loaves or rounds.

div.head: Silver Cake

list.item:
¾ cup butter
2 cups sugar
2 cups pastry flour
4 teaspoons baking powder
¼ teaspoon salt
½ cup milk
8 egg whites
1 teaspoon almond extract

div.p: Follow directions for mixing Butter Cake. Bake in loaves or rounds in moderate oven.

div.head: Nut Cake
div.p: Add one cup chopped walnuts to Silver Cake mixture, and flavor with vanilla instead of almond.

div.head: Orange Cake

list.item:
¼ cup butter
1 cup sugar
2 egg yolks
¼ teaspoon salt
1½ cups flour
2 teaspoons baking powder
½ cup milk
2 egg whites
1 tablespoon orange extract

div.p: Mix as Butter Cake, and bake in two-layer cake pans twenty minutes. Cool, fill with Orange Filling, and cover with Orange Frosting.

div.head: Cream Pie
div.p: Use rule for Orange Cake. Fill with Cream Filling, and sprinkle top with powdered sugar.

div.head: Spice Cake

list.item:
½ cup butter
1½ cups brown sugar
2 eggs
½ cup milk
¼ teaspoon salt
2 cups flour
3 teaspoons baking powder
1 teaspoon cinnamon
½ teaspoon nutmeg
⅛ teaspoon clove

div.p: Mix and sift dry ingredients, add butter, sugar, eggs and milk, and beat until smooth. Bake in a moderate oven forty minutes. One cup chopped raisins, or one cup chopped dates may be added to this cake.

div.head: Marble Cake

list.item:
½ cup butter
1 cup sugar
2 egg yolks
½ cup milk
2 egg whites
½ teaspoon cinnamon
½ teaspoon nutmeg
¼ teaspoon salt
1-¾ cups of flour
3 teaspoons baking powder
1 tablespoon molasses

div.p: Cream butter; add sugar, yolks of eggs beaten until thick, flour in which baking powder has been sifted, alternately with milk and egg whites, beaten until stiff. To one third of this mixture add the spices. Pour into pan the light and dark mixtures irregularly.

div.head: Jelly Roll

list.item:
3 egg yolks
1½ cups sugar
½ cup water
¼ teaspoon salt
2 cups pastry flour
2 teaspoons baking powder
3 egg whites
1 teaspoon vanilla

div.p: Sift baking powder and salt with flour, and follow directions for making Sponge Cake. Pour into medium-sized buttered dripping pan to depth of one half inch. Bake in a moderate oven ten to twelve minutes; turn on to a wet cheese cloth sprinkled with confectioner’s sugar. Cut off edges of cake, spread with warm Jelly, and roll. Work quickly.

div.head: Pound Cake

list.item:
1 pound butter
1 pound sugar
10 eggs
1 pound flour
¼ cup wine
¼ cup brandy
few gratings nutmeg

div.p: Cream butter; add flour. When well blended, add yolks of eggs beaten until thick, then sugar with nutmeg, whites of eggs beaten until stiff, and wine and brandy. Bake in loaves or small cakes.

div.head: Fruit Cake

list.item:
1 pound sugar (brown)
1 pound butter
12 eggs
1 pound flour
½ teaspoon cloves
1 teaspoon each nutmeg and mace
2 teaspoons cinnamon
2 cups raisins
4 cups currants
4 cups chopped almonds
4 cups chopped citron
juice and rind of 1 lemon
¼ cup brandy

div.p: Cream butter; add sugar, eggs well beaten, and remaining ingredients. Pour into buttered and papered pans. Steam three hours and bake two hours.

div.head: Raised Fruit Cake

list.item:
4 cups flour
1 cup butter
1¼ cups sugar
½ cup milk
1 teaspoon salt
½ yeast cake dissolved in one half cup water
2 eggs
¼ cup wine
2 cups seeded raisins
1 cup citron

div.p: Mix all ingredients except eggs and fruit. Raise over night. In the morning add eggs and fruit; cover and raise again; pour into buttered and papered pans; let it rise one hour. Bake in moderate oven one and one half to two hours.

div.head: Imperial Cake

list.item:
¾ cup butter
1½ cups sugar
3 egg yolks
2½ cups flour
3 teaspoons baking powder
¼ cup milk
2 cups seeded raisins
1½ cups currants
1 cup citron
½ cup candied orange peel
¼ cup brandy
3 egg whites
½ teaspoon salt

div.p: Mix as Butter Cake, adding fruit last. Bake in buttered and papered pans in a moderate oven one hour.

div.head: Fig Cake
div.p: Use rule for Orange Cake. Bake in layers. Fill with Fig Filling, and sprinkle with confectioner’s sugar.

div.head: Marshmallow Cake
div.p: Bake Silver Cake in layers. Fill and frost with Marshmallow Frosting.

div.head: Chocolate Marshmallow Cake
div.p: Add four squares melted chocolate to Silver Cake. Bake in layers, and fill and cover with Marshmallow Frosting.

div.head: Mocha Cake
div.p: Use rule for Hot Water Sponge Cake. Bake in layers. Cool; cut in rounds; arrange in three layers, with confectioner’s frosting between; spread sides and top with Mocha Frosting; sprinkle sides with cocoanut, and garnish top with Mocha Frosting put through pastry bag.
If a coffee cake is preferred, substitute hot coffee for hot water in Hot Water Sponge Cake.

div.head: Plain Sponge Cake No. 1

list.item:
8 eggs
½ weight of eggs in flour
weight of eggs in sugar
3 tablespoons lemon juice

div.p: Beat yolks ten minutes; add sugar; beat five minutes; add lemon juice and flour; when well blended, add stiffly beaten whites, cutting and folding them in.
Pour into angel cake pan and bake in a moderate oven one hour.

div.head: Plain Sponge Cake No. 2

list.item:
1 cup powdered sugar
¾ cup flour
¼ teaspoon salt
grated rind ½ lemon
1 tablespoon lemon juice
4 eggs

div.p: Beat yolks until lemon-colored and thick; add sugar, rind and juice of lemon. Cut and fold in the well-beaten whites, also the sifted flour. When thoroughly blended, pour into buttered and papered pan and bake thirty to forty minutes.

div.head: Hot Water Sponge Cake

list.item:
3 egg yolks
1 cup sugar
1 cup flour
1 tablespoon lemon juice
1 teaspoon baking powder
2 tablespoons hot water
3 egg whites
¼ teaspoon salt

div.p: Beat egg yolks until lemon-colored and thick; add sugar and continue beating. Add flour, mixed and sifted with baking powder and salt, hot water, and whites of eggs beaten until stiff, with lemon juice added.

div.head: Simple Chocolate Cake

list.item:
3 eggs
½ cup sugar
¼ teaspoon salt
¼ cup Lowney’s Cocoa
½ teaspoon vanilla
grated rind and juice of ½ lemon
1 tablespoon flour
½ teaspoon cinnamon
½ teaspoon baking powder
¼ teaspoon clove

div.p: Mix cocoa, spice, flour, baking powder, and salt; beat the yolks of eggs until lemon-colored and thick; add sugar and beat well; add lemon juice and rind; when well blended, add chocolate mixture and the beaten whites of eggs. Bake in buttered shallow pans twenty minutes in a moderate oven. When cool put together with Chocolate Frosting or Currant Jelly or White Mountain Cream.

div.head: Cold Water Sponge Cake

list.item:
6 eggs
3 cups sugar
grated rind and juice of ½ lemon
¾ cup cold water
3 cups flour
3 teaspoons baking powder
½ teaspoon salt

div.p: Beat yolks of eggs until lemon-colored and thick; add sugar, rind and juice of lemon, water, flour in which salt and baking powder has been sifted. When well blended, cut and fold in the beaten whites of eggs. Bake in two pans thirty to forty minutes.

div.head: Cream Sponge Cake

list.item:
1 cup sugar
½ cup water
5 egg yolks
grated rind and juice 1 lemon
1⅛ cups flour
5 egg whites

div.p: Cook water and sugar until it threads. Beat egg yolks until lemon-colored and thick. Add sugar sirup, lemon juice and rind, and beat until mixture is cold. Cut and fold in the beaten whites and flour. Bake in an angel cake pan forty to fifty minutes.

div.head: True Sponge Cake

list.item:
6 eggs
1 cup sugar
1 cup flour
juice and rind 1 lemon
⅛ teaspoon salt

div.p: Follow directions for making Sponge Cake. Bake in a deep pan forty to sixty minutes.

div.head: Angel Cake

list.item:
1 cup granulated sugar
1 cup egg whites
1 cup flour
¼ teaspoon salt
1 teaspoon cream of tartar
1 teaspoon vanilla

div.p: Beat egg whites on platter with wire beater. When foamy, add cream of tartar; when stiff, add sugar gradually. Sift flour four times with salt. Cut and fold into egg mixture. Add vanilla, bake one hour in moderate oven in angel cake pan. Invert pan on cake cooler and allow it to drop out itself. If too brown, wrap in wet cheese cloth for ten minutes; then brown may be easily removed.

div.head: Sunshine Cake

list.item:
1 cup sugar
5 egg yolks
¼ teaspoon salt
¾ cup flour
½ teaspoon cream of tartar
6 egg whites
1½ tablespoons orange juice
1 teaspoon lemon juice

div.p: Beat yolks until lemon-colored and thick; add sugar and flavoring and continue beating. Mix and sift flour and cream of tartar four times. Cut and fold in stiffly beaten whites, alternately with flour. Bake in an angel cake pan one hour in a moderate oven.

div.head: Chocolate Cake

list.item:
½ cup butter
1 cup sugar
3 eggs
½ cup milk
2 cups flour
3 teaspoons baking powder
4 ounces chocolate, melted
1 teaspoon vanilla

div.p: Follow rule for mixing Butter Cake and bake in loaf or rounds in moderate oven.

div.head: Almond Cake
div.p: Use rule for Silver Cake. Bake in shallow pan; sprinkle with powdered sugar and chopped almonds. Bake twenty to thirty minutes in moderate oven.

div.head: Bride’s Cake
div.p: Use rule for Silver Cake and bake in angel cake pan forty to sixty minutes.

div.head: Lemon Queens

list.item:
½ cup butter
1 cup sugar
1 cup flour
2 teaspoons baking powder
4 egg yolks
grated rind 1 lemon
2 tablespoons lemon juice
4 egg whites

div.p: Make as Butter Cake and bake in buttered lemon queen pans twenty to thirty minutes.

div.head: Cream Puffs

list.item:
1 cup boiling water
½ cup butter
1-¾ cups flour
5 eggs
1 tablespoon sugar
¼ teaspoon salt

div.p: Boil sugar, water and butter one minute; add flour all at once. Beat until mixture leaves side of the pan in a mass, add eggs, one at a time, beating thoroughly. When all eggs are used, beat five minutes; drop from tip of tablespoon on to a buttered sheet and bake one half hour in quick oven. Fill with Cream Filling, Strawberry Filling, Chocolate Filling, or Whipped Cream.

div.head: Éclairs
div.p: Use rule for Cream Puffs. Put mixture in pastry bag or shape in strips three and one half inches long and one inch wide, on buttered sheet. Bake twenty to thirty minutes in quick oven.
Fill with Cream, Chocolate, Coffee, or Strawberry Filling, and brush tops with melted Fondant, Chocolate Frosting, or Confectioner’s Frosting.

div.head: Lady Fingers

list.item:
6 eggs
¾ cup powdered sugar
1 cup flour
grated rind 1 lemon
⅛ teaspoon salt
powdered sugar
1 tablespoon lemon juice

div.p: Beat yolks until lemon-colored and thick; add sugar and continue beating. Add lemon rind and the egg whites, beaten to a stiff froth. Cut and fold in the flour and salt. Shape on buttered sheet, using tablespoon or pastry bag and tube, four inches long and one inch wide. Sprinkle thickly with powdered sugar.
Bake twelve minutes in a moderately hot oven.

div.head: Sponge Drops
div.p: Use rule for Lady Fingers. Drop from a tablespoon in rounds the size of a silver dollar on buttered sheet. Sprinkle with powdered sugar and bake as Lady Fingers.

div.head: Sugar Cookies

list.item:
½ cup butter
1 cup sugar
1 tablespoon milk
flavoring
2 eggs
2 teaspoons baking powder
¼ teaspoon salt
2 cups flour

div.p: Cream butter; add sugar, yolks well beaten, flour, baking powder, and salt, milk, and whites beaten to a stiff froth, and enough more flour to make of consistency to roll. Cut off a small piece of dough, roll on floured board, sprinkle with granulated sugar, shape with cooky cutter, and bake ten minutes. Save all trimmings until the last. Do not mix trimmings with fresh dough.

div.head: Soft Sugar Cookies

list.item:
1 cup butter
2 cups sugar
2 eggs
⅛ teaspoon salt
1 cup milk
4 cups flour
3 teaspoons baking powder
1 teaspoon lemon extract

div.p: Cream the butter, add sugar, and when creamy the remaining ingredients. Chill. Roll, cut in rounds and bake in a quick oven.

div.head: Sand Cookies

list.item:
½ cup butter
1 cup sugar
1 egg
¼ teaspoon salt
2 cups flour
2 teaspoons baking powder
2 teaspoons cinnamon mixed with
4 tablespoons sugar
½ cup blanched almonds

div.p: Mix as sugar cookies; roll; shape with doughnut cutter; brush with water or white of egg; sprinkle with cinnamon mixture. Decorate with halves of almonds. Bake in a quick oven.

div.head: Nut Cookies

list.item:
¼ cup butter
½ cup sugar
2 eggs
2 teaspoons baking powder
½ teaspoon salt
1 cup flour
¼ cup milk
1 cup chopped nut meats
flavoring

div.p: Mix like Sugar Cookies. Add nuts; drop from a teaspoon on to buttered sheet. Decorate with halves of nuts. Bake in quick oven.

div.head: Almond Cookies

list.item:
½ cup butter
½ cup sugar
1 cup chopped almonds
1 teaspoon cinnamon
3 egg yolks
1½ cups flour
2 teaspoons baking powder
½ teaspoon vanilla

div.p: Mix in the order given. Chill, roll, brush with white of egg, sprinkle with granulated sugar, cut, and bake in a quick oven.

div.head: Bangor Brownies

list.item:
¼ cup butter
1 cup brown sugar
1 egg
3 squares chocolate
½ to ¾ cup flour
1 cup nut meats
¼ teaspoon salt

div.p: Put all ingredients in bowl and beat until well mixed. Spread evenly in buttered baking pan. Bake and cut in strips.

div.head: Creoles

list.item:
3 eggs
1½ cups brown sugar
¾ cup of flour
½ teaspoon salt
1½ cups pecan nut meats
few grains cayenne

div.p: Mix all ingredients in bowl; beat well. Fill small buttered fluted tins one half full. Decorate with pecans. Bake twelve to fifteen minutes.

div.head: Hermits

list.item:
¾ cup butter
1 cup brown sugar
2 eggs
¾ teaspoon soda
1 tablespoon hot water
2½ cups flour
½ teaspoon salt
1 teaspoon cinnamon
¼ teaspoon each, clove, mace and nutmeg
1 cup raisins

div.p: Mix ingredients in order given. Roll mixture one quarter inch thick. Shape with cooky cutter. Put one raisin in center of each round. Bake in moderate oven twelve to fifteen minutes.

div.head: Chocolate Wafers

list.item:
½ cup butter
1 cup sugar
2 eggs
1 teaspoon vanilla
1¼ cups flour
⅛ teaspoon salt
4 tablespoons Lowney’s Premium Chocolate, melted

div.p: Mix in the order given. Beat well. Pour into buttered pans in thin layers. Bake in quick oven six to eight minutes. Cut in long narrow strips while hot, and serve cold.
thick cookies with indentation in center

CHOCOLATE JUMBLES
Plate XIII. For Receipt see page 275

div.head: Wafers

list.item:
½ cup butter
1 cup powdered sugar
½ cup milk
1-¾ cups flour
1 teaspoon vanilla
⅛ teaspoon salt

div.p: Cream the butter and add other ingredients. Spread on inverted buttered tins. Bake in quick oven, cut in squares, and roll. If this is done on top of the range, there will be less danger of the wafers breaking.

div.head: Nut Wafers
div.p: Sprinkle finely chopped nuts on the wafers just before baking.
Look like brownies

CHOCOLATE WALNUT WAFERS
Plate XIV. For Receipt see page 275

div.head: Chocolate Jumbles

list.item:
½ cup butter
1 cup sugar
2 squares Lowney’s Premium Chocolate, grated
2 eggs
2 teaspoons baking powder
2 cups flour and enough more flour to roll out.
1 tablespoon milk

div.p: Mix in the order given, toss on to a floured board, and roll to an inch in thickness. Cut out with a doughnut cutter. Just before putting into the oven, dust over with granulated sugar and bake ten minutes. See colored illustration, Plate XIII, opposite p. 274.
round things with a raisin and chopped nuts on top

LOWNEY’S CHOCOLATE HERMITS
Plate XV. For Receipt see page 275

div.head: Chocolate Walnut Wafers

list.item:
¼ cup butter
½ cup powdered sugar
2 squares Lowney’s Premium Chocolate, grated
¼ cup milk
1 cup flour
½ teaspoon vanilla
1 cup chopped walnuts
½ teaspoon salt

div.p: Cream butter; add dry ingredients, milk and flavoring. Spread on inverted pans which have been well buttered. Sprinkle with chopped nuts. Bake in moderate oven. Crease immediately on removing from oven. See colored illustration, Plate XIV, opposite p. 274.
layered bars with fililng and chopped nuts

CHOCOLATE SWEDISH MERINGUES
Plate XVI. For Receipt see page 276

div.head: Lowney’s Chocolate Hermits

list.item:
½ cup butter
⅔ cup sugar
2 eggs
½ cup raisins seeded
¼ teaspoon salt
2 teaspoons baking powder
2 cups flour
¼ cup Lowney’s Always Ready Chocolate Powder
2 tablespoons hot water
1 teaspoon cinnamon

div.p: Cream butter; add sugar, eggs, raisins, flour in which baking powder has been sifted, chocolate melted in water, salt and cinnamon. Drop from a teaspoon on to a buttered baking sheet, put a raisin in the center of each hermit, and bake in a moderate oven. See colored illustration, Plate XV, opposite p. 275.

div.head: Chocolate Swedish Meringues

list.item:
5 egg whites
½ teaspoon cream of tartar
1 cup sugar
¼ cup Lowney’s Cocoa
½ cup flour
½ teaspoon vanilla

div.p: Beat the whites of eggs until foamy; add cream of tartar, sugar and cocoa. Continue beating until spoon will stand up in mixture; add vanilla and fold in the flour. Bake in buttered shallow pans in a moderate oven about twenty minutes. Put cakes together with following filling, and decorate top with filling and candied fruit and nuts.

div.head: Filling
div.p: Melt one half pound marshmallows. Cook one cup sugar and one third cup boiling water until, when dropped from tip of a spoon, a thread is formed. Pour slowly on to melted marshmallows, add one half teaspoon vanilla, and beat until thick enough to spread. Put between and on top of cakes. Sprinkle with chopped nuts, raisins, cherries and angelica. This may be made in one large cake or cut in small ones the shape of dominoes and decorated in the same way. See colored illustration, Plate XVI, opposite p. 275.

div.head: Cornucopias
div.p: Shape Wafers as soon as taken from the oven. Fill with Whipped Cream, or Cream Fillings of various flavors.

div.head: Chocolate Dominoes

list.item:
½ cup chopped walnut meats
½ cup chopped figs
½ cup almond paste
grated rind of orange
2 squares Lowney’s Premium Chocolate, melted
¼ teaspoon salt
orange juice
sugar

div.p: Mix the ingredients with enough orange juice to make the mixture of the consistency to spread. Knead on a sugared board. Cut in shape of dominoes, coat with melted chocolate, and decorate with pieces of almonds.

div.head: Chocolate Angelettes

list.item:
4 egg whites
½ teaspoon cream of tartar
½ cup sugar
⅛ teaspoon salt
4 tablespoons Lowney’s Always Ready Chocolate Powder
¼ cup flour
1 teaspoon vanilla
confectioner’s sugar

div.p: Beat whites; add cream of tartar and sugar, and continue beating. Cut and fold in salt, chocolate, flour. Flavor and drop by spoonfuls on to a buttered sheet; sprinkle with confectioner’s sugar and bake in a moderate oven.

div.head: Chocolate Cookies

list.item:
½ cup butter
1 cup sugar
1 egg
3 squares Lowney’s Premium Chocolate
2 cups flour
2 teaspoons baking powder
¼ teaspoon salt
4 tablespoons milk

div.p: Cream butter; add remaining ingredients. Chill, roll, and shape. Bake in a moderate oven.

div.head: Chocolate Macaroons

list.item:
½ pound almond paste
⅜ pound powdered sugar
3 egg whites
2 squares Lowney’s Premium Chocolate
⅛ teaspoon salt
1 teaspoon vanilla

div.p: Mix almond paste and sugar, until the mixture feels like meal; add whites of eggs, one at a time, and work with a spatula until there are no lumps; add chocolate, salt and vanilla. Drop from a teaspoon on to a buttered paper; bake twenty to thirty minutes in a slow oven. Remove from paper as soon as cooked. If baked in a quick oven, they will not be a success.

div.head: Cocoa Cocoanut Cookies

list.item:
3 eggs
1 cup sugar
½ cup heavy cream
½ cup shredded cocoanut
¼ cup Lowney’s Always Ready Chocolate Powder
2½ cups flour
2 teaspoons baking powder
1 teaspoon salt

div.p: Mix ingredients in order given. Chill, roll ¼ inch thick, and shape with cooky cutter. Bake in moderate oven.

div.head: Lowney’s Brownies

list.item:
½ cup butter
1 cup sugar
2 squares Lowney’s Premium Chocolate
2 eggs
½ cup nut meats
½ cup flour
¼ teaspoon salt

div.p: Cream butter, add remaining ingredients, spread on buttered sheets, and bake ten to fifteen minutes. Cut in squares as soon as taken from oven.

div.head: Mushroom Meringue
div.p: Make a round of meringue mixture size of a quarter. Shape stems by drawing mixture upward. Sprinkle tops with cocoa. Bake in moderate oven. Remove from paper and press stems into bottom of rounds to resemble mushrooms.

div.head: Macaroons

list.item:
1 cup almond paste
1 cup powdered sugar
3 egg whites
¼ teaspoon almond extract

div.p: Mix almond paste and sugar until like meal. Add one egg white at a time and mix thoroughly. When well blended, shape on buttered paper in small rounds. Bake on inverted dripping pan in a very slow oven. Remove from paper immediately.

div.head: Doughnuts

list.item:
1¼ cups sugar
2 egg yolks
1 egg
1 teaspoon salt
1 cup milk
4½ cups flour
1 teaspoon soda
2 teaspoons cream of tartar
few gratings of nutmeg

div.p: Beat eggs; add sugar, dry ingredients sifted, and milk. Beat well. Add flour to make a soft dough. Chill over night if possible.
Roll to one inch thickness; cut with doughnut cutter; fry in hot fat, turning often. Drain on brown paper.

div.head: Crullers
div.p: Add to doughnut mixture two tablespoons butter. Roll one quarter inch thick. Cut in pieces four inches long and two inches wide. Make two slits in each, twist slightly, and fry in hot fat.

div.head: Hard Gingerbread

list.item:
1½ cups butter
2½ cups sugar
6 eggs
1 teaspoon soda
¼ cup milk
3 teaspoons ginger
8 cups flour

div.p: Cream butter; add remaining ingredients. Spread quarter inch thick on buttered inverted dripping pan. Roll with creased rolling pin. Bake in quick oven. Cut in squares. Cool and keep in air-tight receptacles.

div.head: Molasses Drops

list.item:
⅓ cup butter
⅓ cup boiling water
⅔ cup molasses
1 teaspoon soda
½ teaspoon salt
1 tablespoon ginger
1 teaspoon cinnamon
flour

div.p: Pour boiling water over butter; add remaining ingredients, using sufficient flour to make a drop batter. Drop from tablespoon on to buttered tin. Bake in moderate oven fifteen minutes.

div.head: New York Gingerbread

list.item:
¾ cup butter
1½ cups flour
5 eggs
1-¾ cups powdered sugar
1 tablespoon yellow ginger
1 teaspoon baking powder
¼ teaspoon salt

div.p: Cream butter; add flour. Add remaining ingredients and beat ten minutes. Bake in buttered bread pan forty-five to sixty minutes.

div.head: Meringues

list.item:
1 cup egg whites
¼ teaspoon salt
1 cup fine granulated sugar
½ teaspoon vanilla

div.p: Add salt to eggs; beat until very stiff. Add two tablespoons sugar, beat five minutes. So continue until half the sugar is used. When very stiff, cut and fold in the remaining sugar. Drop by spoonfuls on to wet paper on inverted dripping pan. Bake in slow oven thirty minutes. Remove from paper; take out uncooked portion; dry in oven. Cool and fill with Whipped Cream or Ice Cream. Arrange in pairs.

div.head: Chocolate Meringues
div.p: Substitute one half cup Lowney’s Premium Chocolate for the one half cup cocoanut in the receipt for Cocoanut Meringues.

div.head: Chocolate Cocoanut Meringues
div.p: Add one half cup Lowney’s Premium Chocolate to the receipt for Cocoanut Meringues.

div.head: Cocoanut Meringues

list.item:
4 egg whites
1 cup powdered sugar
⅛ teaspoon salt
½ cup cocoanut
½ teaspoon vanilla

div.p: Beat the whites until dry, add sugar, and continue beating. Cut and fold in remaining ingredients. Shape, using pastry bag and tube. Bake in a very moderate oven.

div.head: Superior Gingerbread

list.item:
⅓ cup butter
1 cup molasses
1 cup boiling water
1 egg
1 teaspoon grated orange peel
3 cups flour
1½ teaspoons soda
½ teaspoon salt
1 teaspoon ginger
1 teaspoon cinnamon

div.p: Mix ingredients in order given. Beat well and bake in loaf thirty minutes, or in muffin pans twenty minutes.

div.head: Sour Milk Gingerbread

list.item:
1 cup molasses
1 cup sour milk
2 cups flour
1 egg
2 teaspoons ginger
2 teaspoons soda
½ teaspoon salt

div.p: Mix and sift dry ingredients; add remaining ingredients, beat well, pour into buttered pan, and bake twenty to thirty minutes.

div.head: Hot Water Gingerbread

list.item:
1 cup molasses
2 cups flour
1 teaspoon soda
1 tablespoon ginger
2 to 4 tablespoons butter or beef suet
½ cup boiling water
½ teaspoon salt
⅛ teaspoon cinnamon

div.p: Mix and sift dry ingredients; add remaining ingredients. Bake twenty to thirty minutes.

div.head: Rochester Gingerbread

list.item:
½ cup beef drippings
½ cup brown sugar
1 cup sour milk
1 cup molasses
2 eggs
3 cups flour
1 teaspoon soda
2 teaspoons ginger

div.p: Melt the beef drippings, add remaining ingredients, beat well, and bake in deep bread pans in a moderate oven.

div.head: Ginger Snaps

list.item:
1 cup molasses
¼ to ½ cup butter, suet, or chicken fat
3 cups flour
½ teaspoon soda
1 tablespoon ginger
2 teaspoons salt

div.p: Boil shortening and molasses two minutes. Add remaining ingredients, mixed and sifted. Beat well; chill over night. Roll very thin. Shape with knife or cutter. Bake on buttered pan in quick oven eight to ten minutes.

div.head: Cocoa Frosting No. 1

list.item:
1 cup confectioners sugar
1 egg white
1 teaspoon flavoring
¼ cup Lowney’s Cocoa
1 tablespoon cream or milk
1 teaspoon butter

div.p: Beat white of egg, sugar and cocoa for five minutes. Add flavoring, milk and melted butter. Spread on cake when cool.

div.head: Cocoa Frosting No. 2

1 cup confectioner’s sugar
4 tablespoons strong coffee
¼ cup Lowney’s Cocoa
⅛ teaspoon salt

div.p: Mix cocoa and sugar; add hot coffee. Stir over fire five minutes. Add salt and spread on cake.

div.head: Rich Chocolate Frosting

list.item:
2 ounces Lowney’s Premium Chocolate
½ cup sugar
2 teaspoons butter
¼ cup milk
1 teaspoon sherry wine, or
½ teaspoon vanilla

div.p: Mix chocolate, add other ingredients, and cook until, when dropped in water, a soft ball is formed.

div.head: Chocolate Frosting

list.item:
2 ounces Lowney’s Premium Chocolate
½ cup cream
1 teaspoon melted butter
1 egg yolk
2 cups confectioner’s sugar
½ teaspoon vanilla

div.p: Melt chocolate, add other ingredients, and spread on cake. One cup chopped walnuts makes a chocolate walnut frosting.
Note.—Confectioner’s sugar varies in thickening properties. Should this frosting be too thick, dilute with a small quantity of hot water or milk.

div.head: Boiled Frosting No. 1

list.item:
1 cup sugar
⅓ cup hot water
1 teaspoon lemon juice
1 egg white
⅛ teaspoon cream of tartar
1 teaspoon vanilla

div.p: Boil sugar and water until it threads; pour on to the beaten egg white, pouring in a steady stream and very slowly, adding, while beating, cream of tartar, lemon juice and vanilla; stir until thick. Spread on cold cake.

div.head: Boiled Frosting No. 2

1 cup sugar
⅓ cup water
2 egg whites

1 teaspoon vanilla

div.p: Follow rule for cooking Boiled Frosting No. 1.

div.head: Confectioner’s Frosting No. 1

list.item:
1 cup confectioner’s sugar
1 egg white
1 teaspoon flavoring extract
½ teaspoon lemon juice

div.p: Mix ingredients and beat until thick.

div.head: Confectioner’s Frosting No. 2
div.p: Same ingredients as Confectioner’s Frosting No. 1, omitting vanilla, and flavoring with strawberry, raspberry, or orange juice.

div.head: Confectioner’s Frosting No. 3

list.item:
3 tablespoons milk, cream, or boiling water
confectioner’s sugar
flavoring extract
1 teaspoon lemon juice

div.p: Add sufficient sugar to liquid to make of consistency to spread; add flavoring and use.

div.head: Caramel Frosting No. 1

list.item:
1 cup brown sugar
⅓ cup cream
few grains salt
3 tablespoons caramelized sugar

div.p: Boil sugar and cream till it begins to thread; add caramelized sugar and spread.

div.head: Caramel Frosting No. 2

list.item:
2 cups brown sugar
1 cup thin cream
1 tablespoon butter
few drops vanilla

div.p: Mix ingredients except vanilla, and boil without stirring until a soft ball can be formed; add vanilla. Beat until creamy. Spread.

div.head: Chocolate Frostings
div.p: See p. 282.

div.head: Coffee Frosting

Confectioner’s Frosting No. 1
2 tablespoons black coffee

1 cup sugar

1 teaspoon vanilla
⅓ cup milk

list.item:

confectioner’s sugar

div.p: Use rule for Fudge Frosting; add one cup shredded cocoanut.

div.p: Boil sugar, water and cream of tartar until thread is formed. Pour on to the beaten white, and continue beating until of consistency to spread.

flavoring

div.p: Boil sugar and water until a soft ball can be formed. Wash sides of saucepan with moist cheese cloth, as fast as the sugar crystallizes. Pour on to marble. When it begins to harden, work with a spatula until creamy. Chill, flavor, melt, and use for frosting.

div.head: Ornamental Frosting

4 egg whites
2 tablespoons lemon juice
confectioner’s sugar
flavoring

div.head: Brown Sugar Frosting

Boiled Frosting

div.head: Mocha Frosting

One cup chopped nuts or one cup shredded cocoanut or one cup mixed fruit may be added to this filling.

div.head: Cocoa Nougat Filling

div.head: Cream Filling

⅛ teaspoon salt

div.head: Curaçoa Filling

div.head: Fig Filling

⅓ cup thin cream
2 egg whites

½ cup chopped almonds

div.head: Maple Filling

list.item:

1 egg white

few grains salt

div.head: Marshmallow Filling

list.item:
½ pound marshmallows
1 egg white

div.head: Lemon Filling

list.item:
2 egg whites
1 cup powdered sugar
2 teaspoons gelatine
2 tablespoons boiling water
1 teaspoon cold water
2 tablespoons lemon juice
grated rind 1 lemon

div.p: Cover gelatine with cold water; dissolve in boiling water; add to beaten whites with sugar, rind and juice.

div.head: Nougat Filling

list.item:
Boiled frosting
1 egg
1 cup chopped nut meats
¼ cup powdered sugar
¼ cup cream

div.p: Beat egg; add powdered sugar, beaten cream and nut meats; add mixture to Boiled Frosting. Beat until thick enough to spread.

div.head: Nut and Raisin Filling

list.item:
1 cup raisins
1 cup chopped nuts
1 egg white
2 tablespoons lemon juice
½ teaspoon salt
½ cup powdered sugar

div.p: Seed raisins and chop until fine; add chopped nuts. Beat egg until stiff; add sugar, nuts, raisins and lemon juice.

div.head: Orange Filling

list.item:
Cream Filling
juice and rind 1 orange
1 tablespoon lemon juice
1 teaspoon butter
½ cup orange pulp

div.p: Mix fruit juice and grated rind, butter, Cream Filling and orange pulp. Spread on cake.

div.head: Fudge Filling

list.item:
2 cups sugar
2 cups rich milk
4 squares chocolate
4 tablespoons butter
1 teaspoon vanilla

div.p: Mix all ingredients and let stand on back of range until mixture liquefies. Boil until a soft ball is formed. Beat until creamy. Spread between cakes.

div.head: Nut Fudge Filling
div.p: Add one cup chopped nuts to Fudge Filling.

div.head: Tutti-frutti Fudge Filling
div.p: Add one and one half cups chopped nuts and candied fruits to Fudge Filling.

div.head: Marshmallow Fudge Filling
div.p: Melt one half pound marshmallows in double boiler and add to Fudge Filling.

div.head: Peach Filling

list.item:
1 cup beaten cream
1 cup powdered sugar
1 cup peach pulp
2 tablespoons lemon juice
few grains salt

div.p: Mix ingredients, spread between cake.

div.head: Pineapple Filling

list.item:
1 cup grated pineapple
1 tablespoon orange rind
2 tablespoons lemon juice
sugar

div.p: Mix pineapple, fruit juice and rind, and enough confectioner’s sugar to make of consistency to spread.

div.head: Directions for Freezing
div.p: Select a reliable freezer and one which runs easily. Keep the gearing well oiled.

Adjust the freezing can in the freezer, making sure that all parts fit and that the crank turns readily. Place ice in bag made of ticking or strong sacking, and with a wooden mallet, pound until very fine. Surround the freezing can with ice and rock salt, using three measures of ice and one of salt, for ice cream and sherbets; two measures of ice and one of salt for sorbets, frappés, etc.; equal measures of ice and of salt for molding and for freezing mousses, bombes, and parfaits.

For freezing ice cream, when the freezing can is cold, pour in mixture to be frozen, let stand five minutes, then turn the crank slowly for eight or ten minutes, then more rapidly until mixture is frozen. Remove dasher, scrape cream from sides of freezing can to the middle and press down so as to have the cream one solid mass; let stand to season, or if to be molded, pack in the mold.
A one-pound baking powder can makes an excellent mold if one has no brick mold.

div.head: Directions for Molding
div.p: Have the mold chilled; press the frozen mixture well into the sides and bottom of mold, packing solidly until overflowing; put on cover, making sure that it fits securely; if in doubt, brush with lard or butter. Tie on cover and immerse in ice and salt, using equal parts of each; let stand one to three hours, depending upon degree of hardness desired. Mousses and parfaits are put directly into the mold, filled to overflowing, covered according to directions, and allowed to stand from four to six hours in ice and salt.
Frozen desserts are divided into:—

Philadelphia ice cream, which is cream sweetened, flavored, and stirred in freezer while freezing; plain ice cream, a custard of different degrees of richness, with or without cream, and stirred while freezing.
Mousses, parfaits and biscuits are made with and without eggs, with beaten or whipped cream, and frozen without stirring.
Water ices are divided into sherbets, frappés, and punch, all stirred while freezing.
Bombes are combinations of ice cream and sherbet, or sherbet and charlotte russe mixture.

div.head: Chocolate Fig Ice Cream

list.item:
4 ounces Lowney’s Premium Chocolate
4 cups cream
¾ cup sugar
1 tablespoon vanilla
½ teaspoon salt
1½ cups finely chopped figs

div.p: Melt chocolate, add sugar and one half cup cream, cook until smooth, add remaining ingredients, and freeze, stirring occasionally while freezing to keep figs from settling to the bottom.
Note.—If figs are soaked in wine, the flavor of the cream is much better, and there is less liability of the figs being lumpy.

div.head: Chocolate Philadelphia Ice Cream

list.item:
2 ounces Lowney’s Premium Chocolate, or
½ cup Lowney’s Cocoa
¼ cup hot water
1 cup sugar
4 cups light cream
¼ teaspoon salt
1 teaspoon vanilla

div.p: Melt chocolate, add remaining ingredients, and freeze.

div.head: Chocolate Junket Ice Cream

list.item:
4 squares Lowney’s Premium Chocolate
2 cups cream
3 cups milk
1 junket tablet
1 tablespoon cold water
1 tablespoon vanilla
1¼ cups sugar

div.p: Scald milk; add melted chocolate and sugar; cook three minutes; cool. When lukewarm, add junket tablet which has been dissolved in cold water. Add cream and freeze.
Two squares of chocolate give a very delicately flavored cream.

div.head: Cocoa Frappé

list.item:
4 cups milk
3 squares Lowney’s Premium Chocolate, or
½ cup Lowney’s Cocoa
½ cup sugar
½ tablespoon arrowroot

1 tablespoon sherry wine
⅛ teaspoon salt
1 inch stick cinnamon

div.p: Mix chocolate, cinnamon, sugar, salt, arrowroot; add milk; cook ten minutes; add vanilla, sherry, and freeze. Serve in frappé glasses, and garnish with cream flavored and beaten, and candied cherries.
Three cups of milk and one cup strong coffee may be used instead of all milk. See colored illustration, Plate XII, opposite p. 263.

div.head: Chocolate Ice Cream No. 1

list.item:
4 cups cream
6 egg yolks
1½ cups sugar
4 ounces Lowney’s Premium Chocolate
¼ teaspoon salt
1 teaspoon vanilla

div.p: Scald one cup of cream; add to melted chocolate and cook three minutes, or until mixture is smooth and glossy; add sugar, salt, vanilla, and the remaining three cups of cream which has been beaten stiff. When well blended, add beaten yolks of eggs. Freeze.

div.head: Chocolate Ice Cream No. 2

list.item:
2 ounces Lowney’s Premium Chocolate
2 tablespoons sugar
2 tablespoons hot water
1 pint cream
2 eggs
½ cup flour
2 cups milk
1 cup sugar
¼ teaspoon salt

div.p: Beat eggs; add flour, one cup sugar, and milk; cook in double boiler twenty minutes. Melt chocolate; add sugar, boiling water; cook until glossy, then add to egg mixture; cool; add cream, salt, and freeze.

div.head: French Ice Cream

list.item:
2 cups milk
2 cups cream
1 cup sugar
4 to 6 egg yolks
1 tablespoon vanilla
¼ teaspoon salt

div.p: Make a soft custard of milk, sugar and yolks of eggs. When cool, add cream whipped, salt and flavoring. Freeze.

div.head: Philadelphia Ice Cream

list.item:
4 cups light cream, or
3 cups heavy cream and one cup milk
1 cup sugar
1 tablespoon flavoring
¼ teaspoon salt

div.p: Mix the ingredients and freeze without cooking.

div.head: Brown Bread Ice Cream
div.p: Add to French Ice Cream one cup brown bread crumbs dried. Freeze.

div.head: Banana Ice Cream
div.p: Add the pulp of four bananas and two tablespoons lemon juice to Philadelphia Ice Cream. Freeze.

div.head: Cocoa Nut Ice Cream

list.item:
2 eggs
1¼ cups sugar
½ cup flour
2 cups milk
½ cup Lowney’s Cocoa
½ teaspoon salt
1 cup walnuts
2 cups cream

div.p: Mix cocoa, flour, sugar and salt; add eggs slightly beaten. When well blended, add scalded milk. Cook in double boiler, stirring constantly, twenty minutes. Add nuts finely chopped, flavoring and cream. Freeze.

div.head: Burnt Almond Ice Cream
div.p: Blanch and chop one cup almonds. Caramelize four tablespoons sugar; add chopped almonds. When cold, pound to a powder. Add to French Ice Cream with one teaspoon almond extract. Freeze.

div.head: Caramel Ice Cream
div.p: Add to French Ice Cream, one cup of caramelized sugar. Cool and freeze.

div.head: Coffee Ice Cream
div.p: Add one cup black coffee to French or Philadelphia Ice Cream. Freeze.

div.head: Ginger Ice Cream
div.p: Add one cup preserved ginger chopped fine, two tablespoons lemon juice, and three tablespoons ginger sirup to Philadelphia or French Ice Cream. Freeze.

div.head: Macaroon Ice Cream
div.p: Add one cup dried and pounded macaroons to French or Philadelphia Ice Cream; flavor with one half teaspoon almond extract, one tablespoon sherry, and one half teaspoon vanilla. Freeze.

div.head: Cocoa Ice Cream

list.item:
2 cups milk
1 cup sugar
1 tablespoon cornstarch or arrowroot
4 egg yolks
2 cups cream, or
2 cups milk and
2 tablespoons butter
¼ to ½ cup Lowney’s Cocoa
1 teaspoon vanilla
¼ teaspoon salt

div.p: Mix cocoa, sugar and cornstarch or arrowroot; add scalded milk, and cook twenty minutes in double boiler. Beat eggs; add cream, or milk and butter; pour on to this mixture, cornstarch mixture. Add vanilla and freeze.
One cup raspberry juice added just before freezing gives a pleasant variety. See colored illustration, Plate XVII, opposite.
looks like very small chocolate volcano

COCOA ICE CREAM
Plate XVII. For Receipt see page 298

div.head: Chocolate Mousse No. 1

list.item:
3 ounces Lowney’s Premium Chocolate
1½ cups sugar
1 cup thin cream
¼ cup cold water
1 teaspoon vanilla
¼ teaspoon salt
whip from 3 cups cream
