1 tablespoon granulated gelatine

div.p: Melt chocolate; add sugar and one cup cream; boil one minute. Mix gelatine with cold water, add to boiling mixture; when cool, add flavoring, salt and whip from cream. Pour into mold, pack in equal parts of ice and salt, let stand four hours. See colored illustration, Plate XVIII, opposite.
A loaf of chocolate, sliced

CHOCOLATE MOUSSE
Plate XVIII. For Receipt see page 298

div.head: Frozen Chocolate

list.item:
4 squares Lowney’s Premium Chocolate
⅓ cup sugar
1 cup boiling water
3 cups scalded milk
½ teaspoon vanilla
¼ teaspoon salt

div.p: Melt chocolate; add sugar, salt and boiling water; cook five minutes; add scalded milk and flavoring; when cool, freeze. Serve with cream sweetened and flavored, either plain or whipped.
looks like moud of whipped cream with caramel sauce

FROZEN CHOCOLATE SOUFFLÉ
Plate XIX. For Receipt see page 299

div.head: Frozen Chocolate Soufflé

list.item:
2 egg yolks
rind and juice of 1 lemon
4 tablespoons sherry wine
½ cup sugar
¼ teaspoon salt
2 egg whites
2 ounces Lowney’s Premium Chocolate, melted
½ cup cream

div.p: Cook first five ingredients until mixture thickens; add beaten whites, chocolate, and cream beaten until thick. Pour into serving dish, and pack in equal parts of ice and salt. Let stand three hours.
A very good way is to put serving dish in lard pail, then surround pail with equal parts of ice and salt.
See colored illustration, Plate XIX, opposite.
cup of ice cream with chocolate sauce

VANILLA ICE CREAM WITH CHOCOLATE SAUCE
Plate XX. For Receipt see pages 247 and 299

div.head: Plain Ice Cream

list.item:
4 cups milk
1 cup sugar
3 eggs
1 tablespoon vanilla
⅛ teaspoon salt

div.p: Prepare as for Soft Custard.
This is the simplest and cheapest ice cream made. One pint of cream added is an improvement.
Freeze according to directions for freezing. See colored illustration, Plate XX, opposite.

div.head: Cocoa Macaroon Ice Cream
div.p: Make a cream the same as for Cocoa Nut Cream, except omit the nuts. Brown in the oven two dozen macaroons. Crumb in meat chopper; add macaroon crumbs and ¼ cup sherry to cream mixture. Freeze.

div.head: Cocoa Cocoanut Cream
div.p: Make a cream the same as for Cocoa Nut Cream, except omit the nuts, and add one cup of shredded cocoanut and the rind and juice of one lemon. Freeze.

div.head: Maple Ice Cream
div.p: Add one cup maple sirup to French or Philadelphia Ice Cream. Freeze and serve with Maple Sauce.

div.head: Nougat Ice Cream
div.p: Add one half cup each of chopped walnuts, almonds, and filberts, to French or Philadelphia Ice Cream. Flavor with one teaspoon vanilla and one teaspoon almond. Freeze.

div.head: Orange Ice Cream
div.p: Add one cup orange juice and one half cup orange pulp to Philadelphia Ice Cream. Flavor with one teaspoon vanilla and one tablespoon lemon juice. Freeze.

div.head: Peach Ice Cream
div.p: Add two cups stewed and strained peaches to Philadelphia Ice Cream. Flavor with one teaspoon lemon juice. Freeze.

div.head: Pineapple Ice Cream
div.p: Add two cups pineapple juice and pulp to French or Philadelphia Ice Cream. Freeze.

div.head: Pistachio Ice Cream
div.p: Mix one half cup Pistachio nuts chopped fine, and one cup almonds chopped fine with Philadelphia Ice Cream. Color a delicate green and flavor with one teaspoon almond. Freeze.

div.head: Plum Pudding Ice Cream
div.p: To Philadelphia Ice Cream add one cup dried and pounded Plum Pudding. Flavor with one tablespoon brandy. Freeze.

div.head: Strawberry Ice Cream
div.p: Add two cups strawberry juice and pulp to Philadelphia Ice Cream. Freeze, and serve with Strawberry Sauce.

div.head: Wine Ice Cream
div.p: Add two tablespoons sherry or Madeira to Philadelphia Ice Cream. Freeze.

div.head: Coffee Mousse

list.item:
1 pint cream
½ cup powdered sugar
1 cup black coffee
¼ teaspoon salt

div.p: Whip the cream, add sugar and coffee, turn mixture into a mold, pack in ice and salt, and let stand five hours.

div.head: Chocolate Mousse No. 2
div.p: Substitute four ounces melted chocolate for coffee in Coffee Mousse, pour into mold, pack in ice and salt, and let stand four hours.

div.head: Strawberry Mousse
div.p: Substitute two cups mashed berries for coffee, and proceed as for Coffee Mousse.

div.head: Fruit Mousses
div.p: Mix two cups of any fruit pulp, with powdered sugar to sweeten, with the whip from one pint cream. A small amount of lemon juice brings out the flavor of other fruits. Mold. Pack and let stand in ice and salt four hours.

div.head: Silver Parfait

list.item:
1 cup sugar
1 cup water
3 egg whites
1 pint cream
flavoring

div.p: Boil sugar and water until it threads. Pour on to the beaten whites of eggs, add the whip from cream, flavoring, pack in ice and salt, and let stand four hours.

div.head: Cocoa Parfait

list.item:
1 cup sugar
½ cup boiling water
4 tablespoons Lowney’s Cocoa
4 egg yolks
2 teaspoons vanilla
2 cups cream
¼ teaspoon salt

div.p: Boil sugar and water together ten minutes; pour sirup on to cocoa which has been beaten with the egg yolks; cook over hot water until of the consistency of soft custard. Beat until cold; add the cream which has been beaten until stiff, vanilla, and salt. Turn into mold, cover, and pack in equal measures of finely crushed ice and rock salt. Let stand four hours. Remove from mold and garnish with cream, sweetened and flavored, and press through the pastry bag.
The parfait may be served in champagne glasses and garnished with beaten cream and candied cherries. See colored illustration, Plate XI, p. 263.

div.head: Golden Parfait

list.item:
1 cup sugar
½ cup water
6 egg yolks
1 pint cream

div.p: Cook sugar and water five minutes. Pour slowly on to the beaten egg yolks, add whip from cream, turn into mold and pack in ice and salt, and let stand four hours.

div.head: Café Parfait
div.p: Add one fourth cup black coffee to Golden Parfait and freeze as Golden Parfait.

div.head: Maple Parfait
div.p: Substitute maple sirup for boiled sugar and water in Golden Parfait. Mold, pack in ice and salt four hours, and serve with chopped browned almonds.

div.head: Nesselrode Pudding
div.p: To Golden Parfait add one cup boiled chestnuts mashed, one cup candied fruit soaked in wine, one cup chopped pineapple. Flavor with one teaspoon vanilla, one tablespoon sherry. Freeze, pack, mold, and serve with Rum Sauce.

div.head: Biscuit Tortoni
div.p: Mix one cup pounded macaroons, two tablespoons sherry, two tablespoons caramelized sugar pounded, with Golden Parfait. Pack in paper boxes, pack boxes in pail, and pack pail in equal parts ice and salt, for four hours. Serve in boxes, sprinkle with brown chopped almonds.

div.head: Biscuit Glacé
div.p: Add two tablespoons maraschino, two tablespoons sherry, to Golden Parfait. Fill paper boxes, pack boxes in pail, pack pail in ice and salt, and let stand in ice and salt four hours.

div.head: Soufflé Glacé

list.item:
1 cup cream
1 tablespoon grated lemon rind
4 eggs
1 cup sugar
½ cup wine
1 tablespoon lemon juice
⅛ teaspoon salt

div.p: Mix yolks of eggs, lemon juice, rind, sugar and salt. Cook until thick. Cool; add beaten whites and cream beaten until stiff. Add wine, fill paper cases, pack cases in pail, and pack pail in ice and salt four hours.

div.head: Plain Water Ice

list.item:
2 cups water
1 cup sugar
4 egg whites
flavoring

div.p: Boil sugar and water; beat until cold. Add egg whites beaten until stiff and flavoring. Freeze.

div.head: Lemon Water Ice
div.p: Add the grated rind of one lemon and the juice of three lemons to Water Ice. Freeze.

div.head: Orange Water Ice
div.p: Add rind of one orange, one half cup orange juice, two tablespoons lemon juice, to Plain Water Ice.

div.head: Pineapple Water Ice
div.p: Add two cups pineapple chopped and pressed through a sieve, with two tablespoons lemon juice, to Plain Water Ice.

div.head: Lemon Sherbet
div.p: The same as Water Ice, omitting the whites of eggs. All fruit sherbets made in the same way.

div.head: Strawberry Bombe Glacé
div.p: Line a mold with Strawberry Ice Cream, fill with Pineapple Water Ice. Pack in ice and salt four hours. Serve with Strawberry Sauce.

div.head: Raspberry Bombe Glacé
div.p: Line a mold with Raspberry Water Ice. Fill with Vanilla Ice Cream, or whipped cream sweetened and flavored. Pack in ice and salt four hours.

div.head: Sultana Roll
div.p: Line sultana roll molds, or one-pound baking powder boxes, with Pistachio Ice Cream. Sprinkle with candied fruit which has been soaked in brandy over night, and fill with Vanilla Ice Cream or with Silver Parfait, or beaten cream sweetened and flavored. Pack in ice and salt four hours. Serve with Claret Sauce.

div.head: Lalla Rookh
div.p: Use rule for Philadelphia Ice Cream. When frozen add one cup Jamaica rum. Serve in glasses.

div.head: Café Frappé

list.item:
3 cups coffee
1 cup sugar
1 cup cream
¼ teaspoon salt

div.p: Freeze to consistency of mush. Serve in frappé glasses with whipped cream on top.

div.head: Orange Frappé

list.item:
1 cup sugar
2 cups water
1 cup orange juice
pulp of four oranges
4 tablespoons lemon juice

div.p: Boil sugar and water five minutes, add other ingredients, and freeze to a mush. Serve with orange sirup and sprinkle with candied orange peel, finely chopped.

div.head: Grape Frappé
div.p: Substitute one cup grape juice for orange juice, and freeze to a mush.

div.head: French Chocolate

list.item:
2 squares Lowney’s Premium Chocolate
½ cup boiling water
⅛ teaspoon salt
3 cups milk scalded
¼ cup ground coffee
2 tablespoons sugar
2 tablespoons brandy

div.p: Melt two squares Lowney’s Premium Chocolate, add sugar and boiling water, boil two minutes. Scald the milk with coffee, strain, and add to chocolate with salt and brandy. Beat with Dover egg beater and serve with beaten cream.

div.head: Plain Chocolate

list.item:
2 squares Lowney’s Premium Chocolate
4 tablespoons sugar
3 cups scalded milk
1 cup boiling water
salt

div.p: Melt two squares Lowney’s Premium Chocolate, add sugar, salt and boiling water; boil two minutes, add scalded milk and beat with Dover egg beater to prevent scum from forming. Serve very hot.

div.head: Emergency Chocolate

list.item:
2 teaspoons Lowney’s Always Ready Chocolate Powder
¼ cup boiling water
1 cup scalded milk
salt

div.p: Mix two teaspoons Lowney’s Always Ready Chocolate Powder with boiling water; boil three minutes, stirring all the time; add scalded milk and cook in double boiler ten minutes; add a few grains of salt and more sugar if needed; beat and serve. This may be made without cooking so long.

div.head: Condensed Milk Chocolate

list.item:
3 squares Lowney’s Premium Chocolate
4 tablespoons sugar
3 cups boiling water
½ can condensed milk
⅛ teaspoon salt

div.p: Melt chocolate; add sugar, salt, and boiling water in which has been mixed the condensed milk. Boil five minutes. If condensed milk has been sweetened, omit sugar.

div.head: Cocoa for Fifty People

list.item:
1½ cups Lowney’s Cocoa
1 quart cold water
2 quarts boiling water
6 quarts scalded milk
¾ cup sugar
2 teaspoons salt

div.p: Mix cocoa, sugar and salt. Add cold water, then boiling water, boil five minutes, add to scalded milk. Beat well with Dover egg beater and serve.

div.head: Chocolate for Fifty People

list.item:
1 pound Lowney’s Chocolate
2 quarts boiling water
¾ pound sugar
6 quarts scalded milk
½ tablespoon salt
1 tablespoon vanilla

div.p: Melt chocolate over hot water, add sugar and water, boil ten minutes. Add salt and scalded milk, beat well. Add vanilla and serve with whipped cream.

div.head: Brandy Cocoa

list.item:
4 tablespoons Lowney’s Breakfast Cocoa
4 tablespoons sugar
1 tablespoon brandy
¼ cup boiling water
4 cups scalded milk
⅛ teaspoon salt

div.p: Mix four tablespoons Lowney’s Breakfast Cocoa, four tablespoons sugar, and one fourth cup boiling water; when smooth, add four cups scalded milk and cook in double boiler twenty minutes; add one tablespoon brandy and salt; beat and serve; garnish with beaten cream.

div.head: Breakfast Cocoa

list.item:
2 tablespoons Lowney’s Breakfast Cocoa
2 cups milk
2 tablespoons sugar
2 cups boiling water
⅛ teaspoon salt

div.p: Mix two tablespoons Lowney’s Breakfast Cocoa, two tablespoons sugar, one eighth teaspoon salt; add two cups boiling water gradually; when smooth, boil five minutes; add two cups scalded milk, beat with a Dover egg beater until frothy.

div.head: Breakfast Cocoa with Condensed Milk

list.item:
4 tablespoons Lowney’s Breakfast Cocoa
2½ cups boiling water
½ cup condensed milk
few grains salt

div.p: Mix four tablespoons Lowney’s Breakfast Cocoa with one cup boiling water; boil two minutes; add one and one half cups boiling water which has been mixed with one half cup condensed milk and a few grains salt; bring to the boiling point and serve with or without whipped cream.
If condensed milk has not been sweetened, add two tablespoons of sugar to the cocoa.

div.head: Tea

list.item:
freshly boiled water
1 teaspoon tea for each cup

div.p: Scald an agate-ware teapot; put in as many teaspoons tea as cups required. Cover with as many cups of boiling water as there are teaspoons of tea. Serve immediately.

div.head: Russian Tea
div.p: Prepare tea, serving a thin slice of lemon and sugar with each cup.

div.head: Tea Punch
div.p: Prepare tea as for Russian Tea and serve with a thin slice of lemon and lump sugar soaked in brandy.

div.head: Iced Tea
div.p: Make tea. Serve in glasses with crushed ice, with one tablespoon lemon juice in each glass.

div.head: Boiled Coffee No. 1

list.item:
1 cup freshly ground coffee
1 whole egg or one egg white
1 cup cold water
6 cups boiling water

div.p: Mix coffee, egg and one half cup cold water, add boiling water, boil hard five minutes. Set on back part of range, add other half cup of cold water, let stand five minutes, and serve with hot milk, cream and sugar.

div.head: Coffee No. 2
div.p: Use rule for Boiled Coffee, using six cups cold water instead of boiling water.

div.head: Coffee No. 3

list.item:
1 cup coffee
6 cups cold water

div.p: Put coffee in cheese cloth bag. Tie, allowing room for coffee to swell. Place in scalded coffee pot, cover with cold water, and boil ten minutes. Remove bag, let stand two minutes on back of range, and serve with hot milk, sugar and cream.

div.head: French Coffee

list.item:
1 cup very finely ground or powdered coffee
6 cups boiling water

div.p: Place coffee in strainer, add boiling water gradually, and refilter, if liked very strong.

div.head: Iced Coffee
div.p: Add hot milk to black coffee, flavor with vanilla, and sweeten to taste. Chill; serve in glasses with a tablespoon of chopped ice in each glass.

div.head: Black Coffee
div.p: Allow two tablespoons of coffee for each cup of boiling water. Always make in French coffee pot.

div.head: After Dinner Coffee

list.item:
1 cup coffee
½ ounce chicory
1 egg slightly beaten
4 cups boiling water
¼ cup cold water

div.p: Mix coffee, chicory, egg and cold water, add boiling water and boil five minutes; let stand five minutes on back of range where it will keep hot. Serve without sugar or cream.
These same ingredients may be used in the French coffee pot, and the liquid may be poured through the coffee until the required strength is obtained.

list.item:
1 pint claret
1 cup curaçoa
1 cup soda water
1 cup sherry
1 slice cucumber
juice of one orange
sugar to taste

2 cups champagne
2 cups soda water
1 bunch mint
1 cup sherry
juice and rind one orange
2 cups Apollinaris
ice
1 tablespoon powdered sugar
1 slice cucumber
juice of one half lemon

2 cups cider
1 cup sherry
½ cup brandy
large piece ice
rind of one lemon
1 slice cucumber
few gratings nutmeg
sugar

div.head: Lemonade
div.p: Boil two cups of sugar and four cups water until a rich sirup is formed. Add one cup lemon juice. Dilute with ice water.

div.head: Orangeade

list.item:
2 cups sugar
2 cups water
⅓ cup lemon juice
⅔ cup orange juice
2 oranges sliced

div.p: Make the same as Lemonade.

div.head: Fruit Punch
div.p: Sufficient to serve twenty-five persons.

list.item:
4 cups sugar
8 cups water
2 quarts Apollinaris
1 pineapple shredded
1 cup fruit juice
1 box strawberries hulled and cut in pieces
4 bananas cut in slices
juice of 6 oranges
juice of 3 lemons

div.p: Boil sugar and water five minutes; add fruit, ice, Apollinaris, and water to make the punch right strength. One cup maraschino cherries may be added.

div.head: Currant Punch

list.item:
4 cups currant juice
4 cups sugar
12 cups water
6 lemons
6 oranges
2 cups tea

div.p: Boil sugar and water five minutes; add tea, juice, lemons and oranges sliced, and a large piece of ice.

div.head: Milk Punch

list.item:
1 cup milk
1 teaspoon sugar
4 teaspoons of sherry, brandy or Madeira
few gratings nutmeg

div.p: Put two lumps of ice in glass; add sugar, milk and wine; shake, strain, and add nutmeg.

div.head: Mint Julep No. 1

list.item:
1 bunch mint
2 cups ice water
juice lemons
2 cups sugar
4 cups water

div.p: Chop mint; add ice water; let stand over night. Boil sugar and water; chill; add lemon juice and mint water. Serve with crushed ice; garnish with mint leaves.

div.head: Mint Julep No. 2
div.p: Put three sprigs mint with one half teaspoon orange bitters in a glass; add one sherry glass Vermouth and one half cup whisky; shake well; add one half cup crushed ice, stir to crush the mint. Add two slices orange, two or three strawberries, and a few sprigs of mint. Add more ice and serve when the outside of the glass is frosted.

div.head: Mulled Wine

list.item:
2 cups water
16 cloves
3 eggs
2 tablespoons sugar
2 cups wine
1 tablespoon lemon juice

div.p: Boil cloves and water ten minutes. Beat yolks and sugar together; add water, wine, lemon juice, and stiffly beaten whites. Serve hot.

div.head:
CHAPTER XVII
FRUITS AND NUTS AND CANDY
Fruits and Nuts
div.p: Fruit is especially wholesome, although not nutritious. The best time to eat fruit is in the morning. Most fruits are improved in flavor by being chilled.
A dish of different fruits attractively arranged makes a very acceptable center piece.

div.head: To prepare Fruit for the Table
div.p: Apples should be washed and wiped dry. Berries should be looked over very carefully, and, if dirty, washed by putting in a colander and allowing cold water to run gently over them, or place the colander in a bowl of cold water and raise up and down several times, then drain thoroughly and chill before serving.
Cherries should be looked over, and served with their stems on.
Bananas should be wiped and chilled.
Currants should be washed and drained, and served on the stem.
Figs, if the dried ones, should be washed, drained, and chilled.

Grape fruit should be cut in halves, the pulp loosened from the skin, and the pith cut out, then chilled; it may be served plain, or sugar and wine may be poured over it just before chilling. Serve one half grape fruit to each person.

Grapes should be washed if dirty, but the bloom is then lost; if picked on one’s own vines, it may not be necessary to wash them; but when bought in the market, it is better to wash and drain, and chill them.
Peaches and plums should be wiped with a soft cloth, and chilled before serving.
Quinces are never served raw.
Strawberries are often served with their hulls on around a mound of sugar; but if they are to be served with sugar and cream, of course they must be hulled and chilled.

Oranges may be chilled and served in the natural state; or prepared the same as grape fruit, and one half served to each person; or peeled and the sections almost, but not quite, separated; or the orange may be cut in the shape of a basket, the pulp removed, the membrane cut off, and the basket refilled with the pulp, which may be sweetened or not.

Pineapples may be served in various ways; perhaps the most popular way is to cut off a slice from the top of the pineapple, then scoop out the center with a fork, and return pulp to pineapple, put on cover, chill, and serve.
Pineapples may be cut in slices, the outer skin be removed, and the tough pith taken out, then serve one or two slices to each person.
If the pineapples are not fully ripe, it is better to remove the skin, pull the pulp in pieces with a fork, then cover with sugar, and chill over night.
Pears should be carefully wiped and chilled before serving.

Melons should be thoroughly chilled. Cantaloupes should be cut in halves, have the seeds removed, and be served one half to a person. Watermelons should be cut in halves, then each half cut in pie-shaped pieces; serve one piece to a person.
Nuts are ordinarily served only at dinner. Hard-shelled nuts should be cracked, served in the shell, or without the shell.
Almonds are cracked, and a portion of the shell discarded, or they may be blanched and salted, and served with the bonbons.
Pecans, filberts, peanuts and walnuts are treated in the same way as almonds.
Castañas or Brazilian nuts are cracked and served in the shell.

div.head: Butter Scotch No. 1

list.item:
3 cups brown sugar
¾ cup water
2 tablespoons butter
⅛ teaspoon soda
1 teaspoon flavoring
few grains salt

div.p: Boil all ingredients until a thread is formed when dropped from a spoon. Pour into hot buttered pans, crease, and let stand until hard.

div.head: Butter Scotch No. 2

list.item:
1 cup brown sugar
1 cup molasses
⅓ cup butter
⅛ teaspoon soda
1 tablespoon vinegar
few grains salt

div.p: Cook in the same way as Butter Scotch No. 1.

div.head: Butter Taffy

list.item:
1 cup molasses
1 cup sugar
⅔ cup butter
⅔ cup milk
1 tablespoon vanilla
few grains salt

div.p: Cook all ingredients until brittle when tried in cold water. Pour into hot buttered pans, crease, and cool.

div.head: Cream Candy

list.item:
2 cups sugar
1 cup water
1 teaspoon cream of tartar
1 teaspoon vanilla

div.p: Cook sugar, water and cream of tartar until brittle when tried in cold water; add vanilla; pour on to greased platter or marble. Pull as soon as it can be handled.

div.head: Cocoanut Candy

list.item:
2 cups sugar
½ cup cream
2 tablespoons butter
1 cup cocoanut

div.p: Cook sugar and cream twelve minutes; add butter and cocoanut. Pour into greased pans, crease, and cool.

div.head: Buttercups

list.item:
2 cups molasses
2 tablespoons butter
1 cup brown sugar
½ cup boiling water

div.p: Cook all ingredients until brittle when tried in cold water. Pour on to hot buttered platter; pull when cool enough to handle; shape in a sheet two inches wide, cover with a layer of fondant, then with a layer of molasses candy, press together and cut in inch pieces.

div.head: Molasses Candy

list.item:
2 cups molasses
2 cups brown sugar
⅓ cup vinegar
1 cup water
2 tablespoons butter
salt

div.p: Boil ingredients until brittle when tried in cold water. Pour into hot buttered pan; pull when cool enough to handle.

div.head: Maple Sugar Candy

list.item:
1 cup maple sugar
½ cup water
1 tablespoon butter
salt
flavoring

div.p: Boil until brittle, pour into greased pan, crease, and cool. One cup nut meats may be added just before pouring into pans.

div.head: Peanut Brittle

list.item:
2 cups sugar
2 cups shelled peanuts

div.p: Melt sugar; when a golden brown, add chopped nuts; pour into hot buttered pan, crease, and cool.

div.head: CANNING AND PRESERVING
div.p: Canned fruits are now more popular with most people than preserved fruits.
The expense in preparing them is less, and the natural flavor is retained.
To prepare fruit for canning, look over carefully, reject imperfect fruit, and be sure that the fruit is clean.

The fruit may be cooked in a saucepan with just enough sugar to make it palatable and water to keep the fruit from burning, and transferred to sterile jars; or it may be put into sterile jars in the first place, and cooked by steam,—the latter method preserves the color and flavor better.

To sterilize jars, put jars into cold water, bring water to the boiling point, and boil ten minutes; fill jars with cooked fruit, and pour in sirup to overflowing; adjust rubbers and covers. Invert and let stand on folded cloth until cold; if there are no air bubbles, place jars in a cool dark closet to keep. If air bubbles are present, take off cover, reheat, and add more hot sirup and proceed as before.

div.head: Canned Apples

list.item:
4 pounds apples
1 pound sugar
2 pints water
juice and rind of 2 lemons

div.p: Pare and core the apples; cover with cold water. Boil sugar and water five minutes; add apples and simmer until tender; add lemon juice and rind; place apples in sterilized jars; fill to overflowing with sirup; adjust rubbers and covers; set in a cool place until cool then keep in dark dry closet.

div.head: Canned Apples and Pineapple

list.item:
4 pounds apples
4 pounds pineapple
2 pounds sugar
2 pints water
rind of 4 lemons

div.p: Pare, core, and cut the apples in rings. Cut pineapple in slices, remove skin and eyes, and cut pulp into squares, being careful to reject the core. Boil sugar and water five minutes; add pineapple; cook until tender; then cook apples until tender; add lemon rind; fill jars which have been sterilized with apple and pineapple, adjust rings, fill jars with sirup, adjust covers, seal.

div.head: Canned Blackberries

list.item:
4 quarts blackberries
2 pints sugar

div.p: Place sugar and berries in preserving kettle, let stand several hours, then cook slowly until the boiling point is reached; boil five minutes; fill sterilized jars and seal.

div.head: Canned Blueberries
div.p: Blueberries are canned the same as Blackberries, allowing one half cup water for every four pounds of blueberries.

div.head: Canned Cherries

list.item:
4 pounds cherries
1 to 2 pounds sugar

div.p: Stone the cherries or not as preferred. Place sugar and cherries in preserving kettle, let stand two hours. Cook until tender, fill sterilized jars, and seal.

div.head: Canned Currants

list.item:
4 pounds currants
4 pounds sugar

div.p: Wash, stem, and cover currants with sugar; let stand in preserving kettle over night. Cook slowly until boiling point is reached, skim, fill sterilized jars, and seal.

div.head: Canned Gooseberries

list.item:
4 pounds gooseberries
2 pounds sugar

div.p: Stem and wash gooseberries, cover with sugar, and let stand over night; if green, add one quarter cup water; bring quickly to boiling point, fill jars, and seal.

div.head: Canned Huckleberries
div.p: Huckleberries are canned in the same way as Blackberries.

div.head: Canned Peaches

list.item:
4 pounds peaches
2 pounds sugar
1 pint water

div.p: Pare peaches and cook in sugar and water, either whole or in halves, until tender. Arrange in jars, fill with sirup, and seal.
Pears, pineapples, and plums are canned in the same way as peaches.

div.head: Canned Quinces

list.item:
4 pounds quinces
2 pounds sugar
1 pint water

div.p: Cook sugar and water until sirupy. Pare and quarter quinces; let stand in cold water. Cook in boiling water until tender, then cook in sugar and water sirup five minutes. Arrange quinces in jars, fill with sirup, and seal.

div.head: Canned Quinces and Apples

list.item:
4 pounds quinces
2 pounds apples
2 pounds sugar
1 quart water

div.p: Pare and quarter quinces and apples, let stand in cold water to prevent discoloration. Cook in boiling water until tender, then simmer in sugar and water sirup ten minutes. Arrange fruit in jars, fill with sirup, and seal.

div.head: Canned Raspberries

list.item:
4 pounds raspberries
2 pounds sugar

div.p: Arrange berries and sugar in alternate layers in glass jars; set jars on trivet in large boiler two thirds full of water; cover and cook until the water in boiler boils vigorously. Remove jar; if berries have settled, refill from another jar, and seal.

div.head: Canned Strawberries
div.p: Prepare in the same way as Canned Raspberries.

div.head: Canned Beans
div.p: Prepare string beans as for boiling. Cook in water one half hour. Fill sterilized jars with beans, adjust rubbers, fill with cold water, and put on covers. Arrange on rack in boiler, fill boiler two thirds full with water, cover boiler, and boil hard two hours. Seal and remove jars.

div.head: Canned Corn
div.p: Cut fresh young corn from the cob. Pack sterilized jars to overflowing with corn. Seal, set on trivet in boiler, surround with cold water, and boil five or six hours, having boiler covered all of the time. Keep in dark, cool place.

div.head: Canned Peas
div.p: Cook shelled peas in boiling water one half hour. Fill sterilized jars with cooked peas, then pour in cold water until jar will hold no more. Set jars on trivet in boiler, surround jars with cold water, cover boiler, and boil four hours. Seal, and keep in cool place.

div.head: Canned Tomatoes
div.p: Remove skins from tomatoes; boil hard twenty minutes; fill sterilized jars, being careful to keep seeds away from rubbers. Seal, and keep in cool place.

div.head: Preserving
div.p: Equal weights or amounts of fruit and sugar are used in preserving.
Select perfect fruit, weigh or measure absolutely accurately, and always cook the fruit long enough to kill all life,—small fruits, one hour, and large fruits until thoroughly tender.

div.head: Preserved Apples

list.item:
4 pounds apples
3 cups water
4 pounds sugar
rind and juice of 6 lemons

div.p: Wash, pare, and quarter apples; keep in water until ready to use. Cook sugar and water five minutes; add apples, cook until tender; add lemon juice and rind. Fill jars with apples, then with sirup, and seal.

div.head: Preserved Crab Apples

list.item:
4 pounds crab apples
4 cups water
4 pounds sugar
juice of 4 lemons

div.p: Wash crab apples, and cook in sugar and water sirup until tender; add lemon juice, fill jars with fruit, then with sirup, and seal.
The fruit is much more attractive if the skin is left on, but may be removed if preferred.

div.head: Preserved Blackberries

list.item:
4 pounds blackberries
4 pounds sugar

div.p: Look over berries and wash. Cover with sugar and let stand two hours. Simmer until the boiling point is reached, boil one minute; cool, bring to the boiling point again, boil one minute; fill jars first with fruit, then with juice, and seal.
Preserved strawberries, raspberries, thimbleberries, and gooseberries are prepared in the same way.

div.head: Preserved Cherries

list.item:
4 pounds cherries
4 pounds sugar

div.p: Wash cherries; remove stems and stones. Cover cherries with sugar, let stand two hours; then set on stove, and bring slowly to the boiling point; cook until cherries are tender. Fill jars first with cherries, then with sirup; seal.
Preserved currants and huckleberries are prepared in the same way.

div.head: Preserved Citron

list.item:
4 pounds citron
4 pounds sugar
4 cups water

div.p: Wash citron, cut in halves, remove seeds; cut each half into eighths, cover with salt, then with water; let stand over night, then drain. Cover with cold water, let stand over night. Drain, remove skin, and cook in sirup of sugar and water until citron is tender. Remove each piece carefully to a platter. When cool, fill jars with citron, and then with boiling sirup. Seal.
If the citron lacks flavor, the juice and rind of four lemons and a small piece of ginger root may be boiled with the sirup.
If the citron is placed in the jars while it is hot, the pieces will not keep their shape.

div.head: Preserved Peaches

list.item:
4 pounds peaches
4 pounds sugar

div.p: Pare, cut in halves, and take out stones. Arrange peaches and sugar in layers in preserving kettle; let stand over night. In morning simmer until peaches are tender; fill jars with fruit, boil sirup five minutes, fill jars with sirup, and seal.

div.head: Preserved Pineapple
div.p: Prepare in the same way as Preserved Peaches.

div.head: Preserved Pears

list.item:
4 pounds pears
4 pounds sugar
2 cups water

div.p: Wash, pare, and cut pears in halves. Put in cold water. Make a syrup of sugar and water; cook only enough pears to fill a jar at a time; when tender fill jars with fruit, then with sirup, and seal.

div.head: Preserved Apricots
div.p: Prepare in the same way as Preserved Pears.

div.head: Preserved Plums

list.item:
4 pounds plums
4 pounds sugar
damsons or green gages or blue plums

div.p: Pick over and prick plums. Arrange alternate layers of plums and sugar in bowl, let stand over night; in the morning drain off sirup, boil, and skim; add plums and cook until tender. Cool plums on platter, fill jars with plums, then with boiling sirup, and seal.

div.head: Preserved Quinces

list.item:
4 pounds quinces
4 pounds sugar
boiling water

div.p: Wash, wipe, pare, core, and cut quinces in quarters. Put in preserving kettle, cover with boiling water. Simmer until tender. Cool on platters. Mix sugar with one pint of water in which quinces have been cooked; boil ten minutes. Add quinces a few at a time, cover kettle, and cook slowly until quinces are of a rich red color. Fill jars with quinces, then with boiling sirup, and seal.
One half quinces and one half apples may be used in this receipt.

div.head: Preserved Green Tomatoes

list.item:
4 quarts green tomatoes
4 lemons
4 pounds sugar
1 inch ginger root
½ cup cold water

div.p: Wash tomatoes and cut in slices; add sliced lemons, sugar, water and ginger root. Simmer two hours, cool, then simmer two hours more. Pour into jars and seal.

div.head: Preserved Ripe Tomatoes
div.p: Prepare in same manner as Preserved Green Tomatoes, except that the tomatoes must have skins removed before slicing them.

div.head: Brandied Peaches

list.item:
4 pounds peaches
2 cups water
4 pounds sugar
2 cups brandy

div.p: Cut peaches in halves, remove stones, and cook in sugar and water sirup five minutes; take out, remove skins, and cook again in sirup five minutes. Remove kettle from range, and let peaches stand in sirup over night. In morning reheat, pack peaches in jars, and fill jars with an equal quantity of sirup and brandy. Seal.

div.head: Brandied Plums
div.p: Prepare in the same manner as Brandied Peaches, but prick plums with knitting needle several times before cooking.

div.head: Peach Butter

list.item:
1 peck peaches
2 quarts cider boiled
2 tablespoons lemon juice
sugar

div.p: Pare and cut peaches in small pieces; add cider and lemon juice, boil until thick, stirring constantly; add sugar, if not sufficiently sweet. Fill jars and seal.

div.head: Grape Butter

list.item:
4 pounds grapes
4 pounds sugar
3 cups vinegar
2 teaspoons each of cloves, nutmeg, cinnamon, and allspice

div.p: Cook all together until thick; press through a sieve to remove seeds. Fill glasses and seal.

div.head: Tutti-frutti

list.item:
1 pound orange pulp
1 pound red currants
1 pound red cherries
1 pound bananas
1 pound pineapple
1 pound apples
1 pound raspberries
1 pound pears
1 pound plums
1 pound peaches
1 pound strawberries
1 pint alcohol
11 pounds sugar

div.p: Put the orange pulp into an earthen crock; add one pound sugar, and two tablespoons alcohol; add this same amount of sugar and alcohol every time a pound of fruit is added. Keep covered with a cloth and tight-fitting cover.

div.head: Apple or Crab Apple Jelly
div.p: Wash and wipe fruit. Remove stems; cut in pieces, put in preserving kettle, nearly cover with cold water; cook very slowly until apples are tender. Pour into jelly bag and drain thoroughly, but do not squeeze. Measure juice, allow one pound of sugar to every pint of juice. Boil juice twenty minutes; add sugar which has been heated on a platter in the oven; stir until sugar is dissolved; boil five minutes or until it jellies. Skim when necessary. Have jelly glasses standing in hot water; pour jelly into them; let stand until hard and cover first with paper or melted paraffine and the tin cover, or paste white paper over the glass. Keep all jellies in cool, dry, dark place.
A rose geranium leaf cooked with the apples gives a pleasant flavor.

div.head: Blackberry Jelly
div.p: Mash blackberries and squeeze in jelly bag. Measure juice, allowing one pound of sugar to each pint of juice. Follow directions for Apple Jelly.
Damson, strawberry, cherry, and raspberry jellies are made in the same way.

div.head: Cranberry Jelly

list.item:
4 cups cranberries
3 cups sugar
½ cup cold water

div.p: Wash cranberries, mash, add water, and boil twenty minutes. Press through sieve, add sugar, and cook three minutes. Pour into glass and cover.

div.head: Cucumber Jelly

list.item:
6 cucumbers
1 quart water
1 ounce gelatine
1 small onion
salt and pepper
1 tablespoon vinegar

div.p: Pare the cucumbers and cut in small pieces. Peel the onion and slice. Cover onion and cucumber with cold water and cook until tender. Press through a sieve, add the gelatine and seasonings. Chill, and serve with Mayonnaise Dressing.

div.head: Currant Jelly
div.p: Wash and drain currants thoroughly. Do not remove stems. Mash a few in the bottom of the kettle. Cook until the juice seems to be extracted from the currants, and the currants look white. Press through a coarse colander, then drip through a jelly bag, but do not squeeze.
Allow one pound of sugar for each pint of juice. Boil juice twenty minutes. Add hot sugar and boil hard three minutes; skim when necessary. Strain into hot glasses; let stand till stiff. Cover.

div.head: Currant and Raspberry Jelly
div.p: Use equal parts of currants and raspberries, and proceed as for Currant Jelly.

div.head: Barberry Jelly
div.p: Use two quarts of apples for every four quarts of barberries and just enough water to keep berries from burning. Follow directions for Currant Jelly.

div.head: Wild Grape Jelly

list.item:
1 peck grapes
1 quart vinegar
4 sour apples
4 tablespoons whole cloves
¼ cup stick cinnamon
brown sugar

div.p: Remove stems from grapes, wash and crush, put in preserve kettle, add all ingredients, except sugar. Cook until mixture begins to look white. Strain through jelly bag. Measure juice, allow one pint of sugar for every pint of juice. Cook juice twenty minutes, add sugar, boil three minutes. Pour into glasses, cover when cold.

div.head: Grape Jelly
div.p: Remove stems from grapes. Mash; boil twenty minutes; strain, but do not squeeze; proceed as for Currant Jelly. Half ripe and half green grapes make the best jelly.

div.head: Mint Jelly
div.p: Follow receipt for Apple Jelly. Allow four sprigs of mint for every four quarts of fruit. When the juice has cooked twenty minutes, color with leaf green, add sugar, and proceed as with Apple Jelly.

div.head: Quince Jelly
div.p: Wipe and cut quinces in thin slices, and follow directions for Apple Jelly.
A delicious jelly is made by using one half quinces and one half Porter apples.

div.head: Apple Ginger

list.item:
4 pounds sour apples
4 lemons
2 pounds sugar
1 ounce white ginger root

div.p: Pare, core, and chop apples; wash, remove seeds, and chop lemons; add sugar and ginger root, and cook very slowly six hours. Pour into glasses and cover.

div.head: Chipped Pears

list.item:
4 pounds pears
½ pound Canton ginger
2 pounds sugar
4 lemons

div.p: Pare, core, and chip pears; wash lemons, remove seeds, and chop; add chopped ginger and sugar; cook very slowly four hours. Pour into glasses and cover.

div.head: Currant and Raspberry Preserve

list.item:
4 pounds currants
4 pounds sugar
4 pounds raspberries

div.p: Remove stems from currants, mash, cook thirty minutes, and strain in jelly bag. Cook sugar and juice ten minutes, add raspberries, bring to the boiling point, fill jars first with berries, then with juice, and seal.

div.head: Apple Marmalade
div.p: Apples with considerable flavor are best for marmalade. Wash, core, and cut apples in slices; put in kettle, add enough water to keep apples from burning. Cook slowly until mushy, press through a sieve, add equal amounts of sugar and apples, and flavor with orange or lemon juice. Cook until water is evaporated; fill glasses, and cover.
All fruits may be made into marmalades by following the above directions. If the fruit lacks flavor, lemon juice, lemon rind, or ginger root may be cooked with the fruit.

div.head: Orange Marmalade No. 1

list.item:
4 pounds oranges
4 pounds sugar
boiling water

div.p: Peel oranges, cut peel in quarters, cover with boiling water, and cook until tender. Drain, scrape to remove white, and cut scraped peel in shreds. Slice oranges, rejecting seeds and stringy portions; add sugar, cook slowly forty minutes; add rind, cook two hours. Pour into jars or glasses. Seal, and keep in cool place.

div.head: Orange Marmalade No. 2

list.item:
4 pounds oranges
6 pounds sugar
6 lemons

div.p: Slice oranges and lemons in very thin slices, reject seeds, cover with sugar, and cook slowly until of a thick consistency, about two hours. Pour into jars or glasses. Seal, and keep in cool place.

div.head: Orange and Rhubarb Marmalade No. 1

list.item:
5 pounds oranges
5 pounds rhubarb
5 pounds sugar
5 lemons
1 quart cold water

div.p: Wash oranges and lemons and slice in thin slices, remove seeds. Cover with cold water, and let stand two hours. Add rhubarb cut in one half inch pieces; cook one hour; add sugar and simmer three hours. Fill glasses, seal, and keep in cool place.

div.head: Orange and Rhubarb Marmalade No. 2

list.item:
5 pounds oranges
5 pounds rhubarb
5 pounds sugar
5 lemons

div.p: Remove skin from oranges and cook in boiling water until soft; drain; scrape off white part and cut peel in strips. Cut oranges and lemons in slices, remove pith and seeds. Cut rhubarb in inch pieces. Cook oranges, lemons, and rhubarb one hour; add sugar and peel and simmer two hours. Pour into glasses and cover when cold.

div.head: Grape Fruit Marmalade No. 1

list.item:
4 pounds grape fruit
4 pounds sugar

div.p: Wash grape fruit, slice thinly, remove seeds and pulpy portion, add sugar, and cook slowly two or three hours. Pour into glasses and cover.

div.head: Grape Fruit Marmalade No. 2

list.item:
6 grape fruits
4 lemons
4 quarts water
10 pounds sugar

div.p: Wash the fruit and cut in thin slices, removing the seeds and as much of the white skin as possible. Cover with water and let stand over night. Cook slowly two hours; add sugar and simmer until thick. Fill glasses, seal, and keep in cool place.

div.head: Peach Marmalade

list.item:
4 pounds peaches
4 pounds sugar
juice 2 lemons

div.p: Wipe and cut peaches in halves, remove stones, cut peaches in pieces; add sugar and cook slowly two hours; add lemon juice. Pour into glasses and cover.
Quince, apricot, plum, and prune marmalade may be made like Peach Marmalade.

div.head: Blackberry Jam

list.item:
4 pounds blackberries
2 pounds sugar

div.p: Wash and pick over blackberries, heat, then press through a sieve. To this purée add sugar and boil one half hour. Pour into glasses and cover.

div.head: Black, Red, or White Currant Jam

list.item:
4 pounds currants
4 pounds sugar

div.p: Stem currants, crush slightly; add sugar, let stand over night; in the morning cook slowly one half hour, stirring often. Turn into glasses and cover.

div.head: Green or Ripe Grape Jam
div.p: Wash and stem grapes. Separate skins from pulp. Cook skins until tender, press through a sieve. Cook pulps ten minutes, press through a sieve. Combine purées; add one pound of sugar to every quart of purée; boil one half hour, stirring often. Pour into glasses and cover.

div.head: Raspberry or Strawberry Jam

list.item:
4 pounds raspberries or strawberries
2½ pounds sugar

div.p: Mash berries; add sugar; cook thirty minutes, stirring very often. Pour into glasses and cover.

div.head: Green Tomato Jam

list.item:
4 pounds green tomatoes
4 pounds loaf sugar
1 cup water
2 ounces preserved ginger

div.p: Wash tomatoes and cut in pieces; add remaining ingredients and cook until clear, about two hours. Strain through coarse strainer to remove seeds. Fill sterilized jars and seal.

div.head: Spiced Currants

list.item:
4 pounds currants
2 tablespoons cinnamon
2 tablespoons clove
2 pounds brown sugar
1 teaspoon salt
1 cup vinegar

div.p: Remove stems and wash currants, add remaining ingredients, and boil twenty minutes. Keep in stone jar.

div.head: Spiced Gooseberries

list.item:
4 pints gooseberries
1 cup vinegar
2 sticks cinnamon
12 cloves
3 pounds brown sugar
1 teaspoon salt
⅛ teaspoon cayenne
1 tablespoon lemon juice
½ ounce ginger root

div.p: Tie spices in bag. Cook vinegar and sugar five minutes. Add spice and remaining ingredients, cook slowly one hour. Keep in stone jar.

div.head: Spiced Peaches

list.item:
4 pounds peaches
1 cup vinegar
1 tablespoon cinnamon
1 tablespoon clove
3 pounds brown sugar
1 teaspoon ginger
1 teaspoon salt
⅛ teaspoon cayenne pepper

div.p: Boil sugar and vinegar. Scald peaches, remove skins, and cook in sirup. Tie spices in bag and cook with peaches. When peaches are tender, pour into stone jars, reheat sirup every day for a week, pouring when boiling over peaches.
All kinds of small fruits may be spiced in this manner.

div.head: Sweet Tomato Pickle

list.item:
4 quarts green tomatoes
4 sliced onions
½ cup salt
1 tablespoon each of clove, mustard and cinnamon
4 cups water
2 pounds brown sugar
2 cups vinegar
¼ teaspoon cayenne

div.p: Slice tomatoes, add onions and salt, and let stand twelve hours. Drain, add water and two cups vinegar, and boil one half hour. Drain; to tomatoes add remaining ingredients, and cook one half hour. Keep in stone jar in cool, dry place.

div.head: PICKLES
div.p: Sweet pickles are prepared from every fruit that can be preserved. Spices are generally tied in a muslin bag and kept in the pickle jar, and the sirup is rich in order to preserve the pickle. Sour pickles should always be cooked in granite or agate-ware kettles, and if desired green, put on to cook in cold vinegar and brought gradually to the boiling point. Alum added to the pickles keeps them crisp.

div.head: Sweet Pickled Watermelon

list.item:
4 cups vinegar
8 pounds sugar
4 tablespoons cinnamon sticks
4 tablespoons cloves (whole)
watermelon

div.p: Cut skin from watermelon; cut rind into small pieces about two inches square; cover with water and cook until tender. Boil sugar and vinegar ten minutes; add spices tied in a bag, simmer until sirupy, about two hours; add melon and simmer one hour. Fill jars and seal.

div.head: Sweet Pickled Pears

list.item:
6 pounds pears
3 pounds sugar
2 cups vinegar
4 tablespoons cloves (whole)
¼ cup mixed spices

div.p: Wash pears, but do not pare. Stick the cloves into the pears. Make a sirup of sugar and vinegar; add spices, when boiling, add a few pears at a time and cook until tender. Fill jars and seal.

div.head: Sweet Pickled Cantaloupe
div.p: Prepare in the same way as Sweet Pickled Watermelon, substituting cantaloupe.

div.head: Sweet Cucumber Pickle
div.p: Soak the cucumbers in a brine for two weeks; drain, and slice lengthwise. Cook in a sirup made by cooking six pounds sugar and four quarts of vinegar; boil twenty minutes. Keep in tightly covered crock.

div.head: Pickled Cucumbers No. 1

list.item:
100 small cucumbers
2 pints salt
1 quart small peppers
8 quarts water

div.p: Boil water and salt together; pour over cucumbers and peppers. Let stand over night; in the morning drain. Make a new brine, using same proportion; repeat this process twice, then drain and wash cucumbers and peppers in cold water. Place cucumbers and peppers in crock; cover with boiling vinegar.
Twelve whole cloves and twelve peppercorns may be tied in a bag and kept in the pickle jar.

div.head: Pickled Cabbage

list.item:
4 quarts chopped cabbage
2 cups chopped onion
1 cup chopped peppers
salt

div.p: Arrange cabbage, onion, and peppers in layers in an earthen crock; cover each layer with salt. Let stand over night; in the morning drain; then arrange cabbage, onion, and peppers in layers, with cloves and mustard seeds. Cover with cider vinegar; let stand twenty-four hours.

div.head: Pickled Cabbage and Celery

list.item:
2 quarts chopped cabbage
1 cup sugar
¼ cup celery seed
2 quarts chopped celery
¼ cup salt
¼ cup mustard seed
3 quarts vinegar

div.p: Cook all ingredients until cabbage is tender. Keep in stone crock.

div.head: Pickled Cucumbers No. 2

list.item:
100 cucumbers sliced
30 small onions sliced
salt
olive oil
vinegar
mustard seed

div.p: Arrange cucumbers and salt in layers and let stand over night. Arrange onions and salt in layers and let stand over night. In the morning drain; put a layer of cucumbers in an earthen crock, cover with olive oil and mustard, then a layer of onions, and so continue until all are used. Cover whole with cider vinegar; let stand covered closely for two months, when it is ready for use.

div.head: Pickled Tomatoes

list.item:
2 quarts chopped tomato
2 cups chopped horse-radish
2 cups chopped celery
½ cup salt
1 tablespoon clove
1 cup chopped onion
½ cup chopped peppers
½ cup mustard seed
½ cup brown sugar
1 tablespoon cinnamon
4 cups vinegar

div.p: Mix all ingredients; stir every morning for a week. Keep in a cool, dark place.

div.head: Mustard Pickle

list.item:
4 cups vinegar
¼ pound mustard seed
¼ pound horse-radish
½ pound mustard
1 cup brown sugar
1 cup chopped green pepper
2 tablespoons turmeric
1 pint button onions
4 cups sliced cucumbers
4 cups sliced green tomatoes
4 cups cauliflower flowerets
2 tablespoons celery seed

div.p: Boil vinegar, spices, and sugar five minutes, add remaining ingredients, and simmer until thick. Keep in crock in cool place.

div.head: Chow Chow

list.item:
1 medium-sized cauliflower
12 green peppers
12 cucumbers (small)
2 cups small onions
2 cups salt
4 cups vinegar
1 teaspoon cayenne
2 quarts boiling water
3 tablespoons mustard

div.p: Peel onions and cook twenty minutes. Drain and cool. Arrange cauliflower, broken in small pieces, cucumbers, peppers and onions in kettle. Cover with brine made of salt and water. Let stand two days. Drain thoroughly, then cover with vinegar, cayenne and mustard. Boil slowly one hour. Keep in Mason or Lightning jars.

div.head: Piccalilli

list.item:
4 dozen small cucumbers
3 quarts small green string beans
4 red peppers
4 green peppers
¼ cup mustard seed
2 heads cabbage
2 heads cauliflower
1 teaspoon ginger
1 teaspoon pepper
1 teaspoon mace
vinegar

div.p: Tie spices in a muslin bag. Chop the vegetables, cover with salt and water, let stand over night. Drain thoroughly, cover with hot vinegar, add spice bag, and let stand until the next morning. Reheat vinegar and pour over pickles; do this for three days, then keep in earthen crock tightly covered.

div.head: Pickled Walnuts
div.p: Run a needle through soft walnuts; cover with strong brine of salt and water; let stand in brine for a week, draining off brine every day, and covering with fresh brine. Then drain and wash walnuts, cover with vinegar, boil ten minutes, add a bag of spices, cover closely, and keep in cool place three weeks.
For bag of spices, mix four tablespoons each of whole cloves, peppercorns, mace, celery and mustard seed.

div.head: Chili Sauce

list.item:
2 dozen tomatoes finely chopped
1 dozen onions finely chopped
1 dozen red peppers finely chopped
1 cup brown sugar
3 cups cider vinegar
¼ cup salt

div.p: Mix all ingredients, add more salt if needed, and boil slowly until thick. Keep in air-tight jars.

div.head: Chutney

list.item:
4 cups sliced sour apples
8 cups chopped green tomatoes
4 cups chopped raisins
1 shallot chopped
¼ cup salt
2 onions chopped
4 cups brown sugar
1 quart vinegar
1 inch ginger root
1 teaspoon cayenne

div.p: Mix all ingredients and cook gently all day. Cool; then boil hard five minutes, stirring constantly. Fill sterilized jars and seal.

div.head: Tomato Ketchup No. 1

list.item:
24 ripe tomatoes
6 onions peeled
6 green peppers
¼ cup salt
¼ cup brown sugar
2 tablespoons ginger
2 tablespoons cinnamon
2 tablespoons mustard
6 cups vinegar

div.p: Peel tomatoes, and cook all ingredients six hours, stirring often. Pour into sterilized bottles and seal.

div.head: Tomato Ketchup No. 2

list.item:
½ bushel tomatoes
2 tablespoons mustard
2 tablespoons ginger
1 tablespoon cloves
1 tablespoon allspice
2 tablespoons pepper
3 quarts vinegar
2 cups alcohol
3 cups brown sugar
1 cup salt
2 lemons finely chopped
cayenne pepper

div.p: Cook tomatoes one hour; press through a sieve; add all ingredients, except alcohol, and cook until thick; boil one minute; add alcohol, and bottle. The cooking will take six or eight hours; stir occasionally to keep from burning.

div.head: Mushroom Ketchup
div.p: Arrange layers of mushrooms and salt in preserving kettle; let stand on back of stove for twelve hours. Press through a sieve. Measure. For each quart of mushroom liquor add one pint vinegar, one tablespoon salt, two tablespoons each of cloves, allspice, mace, and mustard seed. Boil until thick, then bottle.

div.head: Cucumber Ketchup

list.item:
3 large cucumbers
1 large onion
2 tablespoons grated horse-radish
2 tablespoons salt
2 cups vinegar
2 tablespoons pepper
1 teaspoon paprika

div.p: Grate cucumber and onion, add remaining ingredients, boil five minutes, bottle, and seal.

div.head: Rhubarb Wine

list.item:
8 pounds rhubarb
grated rind of 4 lemons
8 quarts water
6 pounds sugar

div.p: Chop the rhubarb; add lemon rind and water; let stand three days. Strain, add sugar, pour into crock, cover with muslin, let stand for two weeks. Cover tightly, at the end of a month it will be ready to bottle.

div.head: Grape Juice

list.item:
6 pounds grapes
3 cups cold water

div.p: Wash and mash grapes; add water and boil ten minutes; strain. For every quart of juice add two cups sugar. Boil sugar and juice eight minutes, bottle and seal while hot.

div.head: Red Pepper Relish

list.item:
8 quarts red pepper
2 quarts vinegar
4 pounds brown sugar
1 teaspoon salt

div.p: Remove seeds from peppers; cut peppers in narrow strips, using scissors. Cover with boiling water, keep on back of range ten minutes, but do not boil. Drain, cover with ice water, and let stand ten minutes. Repeat this process twice. Boil sugar, vinegar and salt twenty minutes. Drain peppers, pack sterilized jars with peppers, add sirup to fill jars. Seal and keep in cold place.

div.head:
CHAPTER XIX
CHAFING DISH DELICACIES
div.p: The chafing dish is composed of the blazer and hot water pan, set in a standard with a small lamp underneath. Some lamps have an electric attachment, but alcohol is the fuel most used. The best alcohol is the most satisfactory, although many use wood alcohol.
Every kind of dish which is usually prepared in a saucepan or double boiler can be made in the chafing dish, but ordinarily oyster, mushroom, fish, egg, and cheese dishes are the ones most popular.

When preparing for a chafing dish supper, arrange the chafing dish on a tray, have the lamp filled, and matches at hand. A wooden spoon or regular chafing dish spoon and a wire whisk are convenient and really necessary utensils. It is well to have all the ingredients measured and neatly arranged on a tray. If butter is to be used, butter balls, each representing a tablespoon, are a convenient and attractive way in which to serve it.
If toast is to be used, have the bread cut in small rounds or triangles and toasted a golden brown. It should be kept hot until ready to be used.
Light the lamp and have the water boiling before the supper is announced, then the compounding of the dish may be done quickly.

div.head: Salted Almonds
div.p: Heat one tablespoon olive oil in chafing dish; add one cup blanched and dried almonds. Stir until evenly colored. Drain and sprinkle with salt.

div.head: Deviled Almonds
div.p: Melt one tablespoon butter in chafing dish. Add one tablespoon chopped red pepper, one tablespoon onion, one half teaspoon salt, and one cup blanched almonds. Cook until almonds are brown.

div.head: Deviled Beef
div.p: Melt two tablespoons butter, add two tablespoons green pepper, one tablespoon onion, one teaspoon each of salt and lemon juice, one tablespoon flour. Spread on rounds of cold roast beef and sauté in butter; or add one half cup tomato and reheat beef in sauce.

div.head: Bacon and Chicken Livers
div.p: Cut six chicken livers in slices, sprinkle with salt and pepper. Add an equal amount of sliced bacon. Cook together until livers are tender. Add two tablespoons flour, one half teaspoon salt, one cup stock or tomato. Season with Worcestershire and serve hot on toast.

div.head: Bacon and Mushrooms
div.p: Wrap eight mushrooms in eight slices of bacon. Cook in chafing dish until mushrooms are tender. Sprinkle with salt and pepper and serve.

div.head: Chicken Livers with Mushrooms
div.p: Make a Brown Sauce; add two cups sliced cooked livers and one cup chopped mushrooms. Reheat and serve on toast. Two tablespoons wine may be added.

div.head: Deviled Bananas
div.p: Melt one tablespoon butter, add one tablespoon chopped red pepper, two teaspoons chopped pickles, one teaspoon Worcestershire sauce, one fourth teaspoon salt. Add four bananas cut in four equal parts. Cook five minutes.

div.head: Frizzled Beef
div.p: Melt one tablespoon butter, add one tablespoon flour and one half pound dried beef. Cook five minutes, add one half cup stock, few drops onion juice, one half teaspoon Worcestershire Sauce, two eggs well beaten. Cook two minutes and serve.

div.head: Beef with Currant Jelly Sauce
div.p: Make Brown Sauce; add one cup Currant Jelly and twelve thin slices rare roast beef. Cook until hot and serve.

div.head: Cheese Dreams
div.p: Cut twelve thin slices of bread and remove crusts. Cut in halves, cover with a thin slice of American cheese, sprinkle with salt, paprika and cayenne; cover with another slice of bread and sauté on both sides in butter. These are more easily prepared small than large.

div.head: Cheese Custard
div.p: Melt two tablespoons butter; add one teaspoon each of salt, mustard and paprika. Add two cups cheese, one half cup soft bread crumbs, and one cup milk. Cook five minutes. Add two eggs well beaten; when thoroughly blended, pour on to bread toasted on one side.

div.head: Cheese Omelet
div.p: Melt one tablespoon butter; add four eggs slightly beaten, four tablespoons milk, one half teaspoon salt, one cup grated cheese. Cook like a French Omelet over hot water. Serve with or without Tomato Sauce.

div.head: Welsh Rarebit
div.p: Melt one teaspoon butter, add one teaspoon each of salt, mustard and paprika; add two cups American cheese. When melted, add one half cup cream or ale. Stir vigorously until smooth, and pour over hot buttered crackers or toast.

div.head: Cheese and Tomato Rarebit
div.p: Melt one tablespoon butter; add three sliced tomatoes, one half cup milk, one teaspoon salt, two cups cheese. Stir continually until cheese is melted. Add three eggs well beaten. When hot, serve on hot buttered toast.

div.head: Cheese with Red Peppers
div.p: Melt two tablespoons butter, add four tablespoons chopped pepper, one half tablespoon chopped onion, one fourth cup grated cheese, one fourth cup cream, four eggs slightly beaten. Cook until well blended and serve on buttered slices of toast.

div.head: Chicken à la Crême
div.p: Make a White Sauce; add one and one half cups chicken meat, cut in cubes, one half cup mushrooms, cut in slices, and one red pepper, finely chopped. Add more seasoning if required and serve on hot toast.
Turkey, veal, lamb, or game may be served in this way.

div.head: Chicken and Mushrooms à la Crême
div.p: Melt two tablespoons butter; add two tablespoons flour, one cup cream, one half teaspoon salt. Add one cup each of cold cooked chicken, cut in pieces, and cooked mushrooms, also cut in pieces.
Serve very hot on buttered toast. A few drops of Tabasco may be added.

div.head: Curried Chicken
div.p: Add one tablespoon curry powder to Chicken à la Crême.

div.head: Chicken with Hard-cooked Eggs
div.p: Cut four hard-cooked eggs in slices, add to two cups creamed chicken with two tablespoons sherry.

div.head: Béchamel Eggs
div.p: Two cups Béchamel Sauce, mixed with four hard-cooked eggs, cut in slices; one half cup sautéd mushrooms. Cook all together five minutes; serve on hot toast.

div.head: Creamed Eggs
div.p: Melt two tablespoons butter; add two tablespoons flour, one fourth teaspoon salt, few grains cayenne, one cup cream. Cook until thick, add two egg yolks and six hard-cooked eggs, cut in pieces, and serve hot on toast.

div.head: Scrambled Eggs and Tomato
div.p: Melt two tablespoons butter; add one tablespoon each of chopped pepper and onion, one cup cooked tomato, one half teaspoon salt. When hot, add four eggs slightly beaten; when scrambled, serve on toast.

div.head: Poached Eggs on Toast
div.p: May be prepared in chafing dish.

div.head: Creamed Lobster
div.p: Melt two tablespoons butter; add one fourth teaspoon salt, few grains cayenne, two tablespoons flour, one cup cream, few gratings nutmeg. Cook ten minutes, add meat from a two-pound lobster cut in small pieces, the grated coral, and one tablespoon butter. One teaspoon Worcestershire and one teaspoon mustard may be added.

div.head: Lobster à la Newburg
div.p: Melt two tablespoons butter; add one tablespoon flour, one teaspoon salt, few grains cayenne, one cup cream. Cook five minutes; add three egg yolks well beaten, the meat from a two-pound lobster, and just before serving, two tablespoons each of sherry and brandy.

div.head: Lobster with Pimolas
div.p: Mix one cup Brown Sauce, one cup sliced pimolas, two hard-cooked eggs cut in slices, one fourth teaspoon salt, few gratings nutmeg, and two tablespoons sautéd mushrooms, with two cups lobster meat. Serve when hot with slices of brown bread toast.

div.head: Lobster with Mushrooms
div.p: Melt three tablespoons butter; add one cup fresh mushrooms, cut in slices, few drops onion juice, two tablespoons flour, one cup cream or Chicken Stock; meat from a two-pound lobster and salt, pepper, and cayenne to taste. Serve when hot.

div.head: Lamb Terrapin
div.p: Mix two cups cold cooked lamb, cut in small pieces, two hard-cooked eggs, chopped fine, two tablespoons olive oil. Let stand two minutes. Melt two tablespoons butter; add two tablespoons flour, one teaspoon mustard, one teaspoon Worcestershire Sauce, and one cup Lamb Stock, or milk. Cook five minutes. Add lamb and eggs and serve on graham toast.

div.head: Sautéd Oysters
div.p: Season four dozen large oysters with salt, pepper, onion juice and lemon juice. Dip in crumbs, egg and crumbs, and sauté in butter.

div.head: Fricassee of Oysters and Mushrooms
div.p: Melt two tablespoons butter; add one tablespoon flour, one half finely chopped onion, one cup mushrooms, broken in small pieces, one cup Chicken Stock or one cup oyster liquor. Cook five minutes and add two cups oysters drained from their liquor. Reheat; season with salt, pepper, cayenne and Worcestershire Sauce. Serve with Brown Bread Sandwiches.

div.head: Celeried Oysters
div.p: Melt two tablespoons butter; add two cups each of celery and oysters. Season with salt, cayenne and lemon juice. Serve hot with crisp toast.

div.head: Shrimps and Tomatoes
div.p: Melt two tablespoons butter; add one can tomatoes; simmer until of purée consistency. Season highly with salt, pepper and onion juice. Add two cups shrimps which have been marinated in French Dressing for one hour. When hot, serve on hot buttered toast.

div.head: Sweetbreads with Bacon
div.p: Cut cooked sweetbreads in inch pieces. Sprinkle with salt, cayenne, lemon juice and onion juice. Wrap in slices of bacon. Skewer, sauté in butter. Serve with Brown Sauce, and garnish with finely chopped celery.

div.head: Calves’ Brains à la Béchamel
div.p: Cut two cups cooked brains in small pieces. Marinate with French Dressing. Melt two tablespoons butter; add four tablespoons chopped peppers, one half cup chopped mushrooms, few drops onion juice, two tablespoons flour, and one cup Chicken Stock. Cook five minutes; add brains; season with salt, cayenne, Tabasco and Worcestershire.

div.head: Buttered Tomatoes
div.p: Melt one half cup butter; sprinkle six sliced tomatoes with salt and pepper; put in chafing dish; cover and cook twenty minutes. Serve on toast.

div.head: Venison with Currant Jelly
div.p: Melt two tablespoons butter; add one quarter teaspoon salt, few grains cayenne, one tablespoon lemon juice, one cup Currant Jelly, one half cup sherry; cook five minutes. Keep hot while cooking slice of venison steak in chafing dish eight minutes. Serve sauce with venison.

div.head: Venison Stew
div.p: Cut one slice venison steak in inch pieces. Cover with Chicken or Veal Stock; simmer until tender, about fifteen minutes; season with salt and pepper; add one cup Currant Jelly and serve.

div.head: Sautéd Bananas
div.p: Peel and cut four bananas in four pieces; melt two tablespoons butter, add two tablespoons sugar, and one half cup sherry; when hot, add bananas, and cook until bananas are hot and tender.

div.head: Hot Fruit Salad
div.p: Melt two tablespoons butter; add four tablespoons sugar, one quarter cup water, and one quarter cup lemon juice; add two cups mixed fruit, apples, bananas, figs and cherries; when hot, serve with cream sweetened and beaten until stiff.

div.head: Peach Canapé
div.p: Melt two tablespoons butter; add two cups peaches with skin and stones removed; cook ten minutes; add sugar and lemon juice, and serve on slices of sautéd bread or Sponge Cake; garnish with cream.

div.head: Pineapple Canapé
div.p: Substitute two cups shredded pineapple for peaches, and follow directions for Peach Canapé.

div.head:
CHAPTER XX
COOKERY FOR THE SICK AND CONVALESCENT
div.p: The preparation of food for the sick and convalescent person is even more important than the preparation for the strong and well. Certain points should always be considered. The food should be freshly prepared, daintily served, and if possible different dishes for each meal.

The arrangement of the tray is often of great importance. Select attractive dishes and arrange them so that the patient can reach them without trouble. Serve everything which should be hot, very hot, and cold dishes, ice cold.

div.head: Apple Water

list.item:
1 large juicy apple
2 cups water
sugar

div.p: Wash, pare, core, and cut apple into pieces; add water and simmer until tender; strain, add sugar to water, cook five minutes, chill, and serve. If apple is not tart, a small amount of lemon juice may be added to give a more agreeable flavor.
Pears, peaches, plums, figs, prunes, raisins, and rhubarb may be used in the same way.

div.head: Barley Water

list.item:
2 cups boiling water
½ tablespoon prepared barley
salt
sugar

div.p: Mix barley with a small amount of cold water, add to boiling water, and simmer twenty minutes. Season with salt and sugar. Lemon juice may be added if desired.

div.head: Cinnamon Water

list.item:
½ ounce stick cinnamon
2 cups boiling water

div.p: Break cinnamon in small pieces, add water, and boil twenty minutes. Strain and serve hot or cold.

div.head: Currant Water

list.item:
2 tablespoons Currant Jelly
1 cup boiling water

div.p: Mix jelly and water, strain, chill, and serve.
Cranberry, strawberry, raspberry, blackberry, and plum water may be prepared in the same way.

div.head: Distilled Water
div.p: This may be prepared at home by attaching one end of a curved tube to the spout of the teakettle, and having the other end placed in a jar. The jar should be placed in a kettle of cold water. This condensed steam is distilled water.

div.head: Flaxseed Tea

list.item:
½ cup flaxseed
salt
4 cups boiling water
sugar
lemon juice

div.p: Boil flaxseed and water one hour, strain, sweeten, and flavor. Serve hot or cold.

div.head: Grape Water

list.item:
2 cups grapes
1½ cups boiling water

div.p: Wash grapes, mash, add water, simmer ten minutes, strain, chill, and serve.

div.head: Lemonade

list.item:
2 tablespoons lemon juice
2 tablespoons Sugar Sirup
1 cup cold water

div.p: Mix ingredients, add crushed ice, and serve ice-cold with straws.

div.head: Oatmeal Water

list.item:
4 tablespoons fine oatmeal
4 cups boiling water
salt

div.p: Boil all ingredients twenty minutes, strain, cool, add water to make of pleasant consistency.

div.head: Tamarind Water

list.item:
1 tablespoon tamarinds
1 cup boiling water

div.p: Let tamarinds stand in water one half hour, strain, chill, and serve.

div.head: Toast Water
div.p: Dry and brown in the oven very thin slices of white or graham bread, break into small pieces, cover with boiling water; when cold, strain and season with salt.

div.head: Sugar Sirup

list.item:
1 cup sugar
½ cup boiling water

div.p: Boil two minutes, keep in preserve jar, and use when needed.

div.head: Irish Moss Lemonade

list.item:
4 tablespoons Irish Moss
2 cups cold water
3 tablespoons lemon juice
Sugar Sirup

div.p: Pick over and soak moss in cold water to cover for one half hour; drain, cover with two cups cold water, and cook ten minutes; strain, add lemon juice and Sugar Sirup to taste.

div.head: Milk Punch

list.item:
¾ cup fresh milk
salt
2 tablespoons brandy or whisky
nutmeg
sugar

div.p: Sweeten milk to taste, add salt and liquor, and pour from one tumbler to another until frothy.

div.head: Egg and Milk Punch

list.item:
1 egg
¾ cup milk
1 tablespoon whisky or brandy
2 teaspoons sugar

div.p: Beat yolk; add milk, liquor and sugar, pour into glass; add well-beaten white of egg, stir lightly, and serve.

div.head: Eggnog

list.item:
1 egg
1 teaspoon sugar
salt
2 tablespoons wine, whisky or brandy
1 cup cream

div.p: Beat white of egg until stiff; add beaten cream and liquor, then well-beaten yolk mixed with sugar and salt.
Milk or hot water may be substituted for the cream, and the yolk and white may be beaten together just slightly if a foamy eggnog is disliked.

div.head: Koumiss
div.p: Heat four cups milk; cool; when lukewarm, add one fourth yeast cake dissolved in one fourth cup lukewarm water, and two tablespoons sugar. Pour into bottles with patent stoppers, fill two thirds full, cork tightly. Shake; let stand in kitchen six hours, then on ice for twenty-four hours; serve ice cold.

div.head: Egg Cordial

list.item:
1 egg white
1 tablespoon brandy or wine
1 teaspoon sugar
few grains salt
2 tablespoons cream

div.p: Beat white until frothy; add cream and continue beating; add remaining ingredients and serve immediately.

div.head: Orange Egg Cordial
div.p: Prepare as Egg Cordial, omitting wine and cream, and using the juice of one orange.

div.head: Albuminized Milk

list.item:
1 egg white
½ cup milk
salt

div.p: Beat white until frothy; add salt and milk, and continue beating; strain and serve.

div.head: Egg and Lemon

list.item:
1 egg
salt
3 tablespoons lemon juice
1 teaspoon sugar

div.p: Beat egg, add remaining ingredients, and serve cold.

div.head: Wine Whey

list.item:
2 cups milk
½ cup wine

div.p: Scald milk; add wine; let stand until curds separate from whey. Strain and serve hot or cold. Lemon or Vinegar Whey may be prepared in the same way; allow one tablespoon vinegar or two tablespoons lemon juice.

div.head: Barley Gruel

list.item:
1 tablespoon barley flour
¼ cup cold water
½ cup boiling water
½ cup milk
salt

div.p: Mix barley with cold water and salt; add boiling water and cook in double boiler one half hour; add milk and cook ten minutes more; if too thick, thin with hot milk or cream.

div.head: Entire Wheat Gruel

list.item:
¼ cup entire wheat
½ cup cold water
3 cups water (hot)
salt

div.p: Mix wheat and cold water, add boiling water and salt, and cook in double boiler one to two hours. Milk may be substituted for water.

div.head: Cracker Gruel

list.item:
2 tablespoons cracker crumbs
1 cup milk
¼ teaspoon salt

div.p: Mix crumbs and milk and cook in double boiler twenty minutes; add salt and serve.
Dried bread crumbs may be substituted for cracker crumbs.

div.head: Corn Meal Gruel

list.item:
2 tablespoons corn meal
¼ teaspoon salt
½ cup milk
2 cups boiling water

div.p: Mix corn meal, salt and milk; add boiling water and cook in double boiler two hours.

div.head: Flour Gruel

list.item:
2 tablespoons flour
¼ cup cold water
2 cups scalded milk
¼ teaspoon salt

div.p: Mix flour with cold water, add scalded milk and salt. Cook in a double boiler thirty minutes, stirring often.

div.head: Flour Ball for Flour Gruel
div.p: Knead two cups flour into a ball, adding water to form a stiff dough. Tie ball in a linen cloth and boil in deep saucepan ten to twelve hours, keeping the cloth covered with boiling water all of the time. Dry in cloth, remove cloth, and dry ball in oven. This will keep for years. Scrape two tablespoons from the ball; add one fourth cup cold water and two cups scalded milk; cook in double boiler ten minutes, add salt, and serve.

div.head: Oatmeal Gruel

list.item:
2 tablespoons oatmeal
2 cups boiling water
¼ cup cold water
⅛ teaspoon salt

div.p: Mix oatmeal with cold water; add salt and boiling water, and cook two hours, or better still over night, in double boiler. Strain and serve; thin with hot water or milk if not of the desired consistency.

div.head: Oatmeal Caudle
div.p: Add one egg yolk and one tablespoon brandy or sherry to Oatmeal Gruel.

div.head: Rice Gruel

list.item:
2 tablespoons ground rice
¼ cup cold water
2 cups milk
¼ teaspoon salt

div.p: Mix rice and cold water; add scalded milk and cook in double boiler two hours, stirring occasionally. Strain, add salt, and serve.

div.head: Dry Toast
div.p: Cut stale bread in one quarter inch slices; remove crust or not as preferred. Dry in oven; place on toaster and toast over clear fire, first on one side and then on the other, having both sides a golden brown. Arrange in toast rack or cover with napkin.

div.head: Buttered Toast
div.p: Prepare bread as for Dry Toast, and spread with butter as soon as taken from toaster.

div.head: Water Toast
div.p: Prepare bread as for Dry Toast, dip in hot salted water, drain, and spread with butter.

div.head: Milk Toast

list.item:
3 cups scalded milk
3 tablespoons butter
¼ cup cold milk
3 tablespoons flour
½ teaspoon salt
toasted bread

div.p: Toast bread according to receipt for Dry Toast. Mix flour and cold milk; add to scalded milk and cook in double boiler twenty minutes, stirring constantly at first; add salt and butter; dip toast in sauce; serve in hot dish; add remaining sauce.

div.head: Cream Toast
div.p: Prepare in the same way as Milk Toast, substituting cream for milk.

div.head: Brown Bread Toast
div.p: Cut brown bread in thin slices; dry in oven, then toast; butter each slice, and cover with scalded milk.

div.head: Pulled Bread
div.p: Remove the crust from fresh bread and tear the center in small pieces. Dry in slow oven; the center of biscuits may be prepared in the same way.

div.head: Bread and Butter Sandwiches
div.p: Cut bread in thin slices; remove crusts; spread with creamed butter; put two slices together; cut in desired shapes. Arrange on fancy plate.

div.head: Raw Beef Sandwiches
div.p: Cut bread in thin slices; remove crusts; shape and spread with raw beef. Serve as soon as made.

div.head: To scrape Raw Beef
div.p: Buy bottom or top of round of beef; wipe, then scrape with a teaspoon; there should be nothing but fiber left when all meat is scraped.

div.head: Fig Sandwiches
div.p: Fill bread and butter sandwiches with stewed figs.

div.head: Beef Juice
div.p: Buy one half pound from top of round; wipe, and set in oven five minutes; cut in thin slices, squeeze, using meat press or lemon squeezer. Serve in warm, not hot cups, with salt or not.

div.head: Beef Tea
div.p: Wipe one half pound of round steak; remove all fat; cut in small pieces; add one cup cold water; place in preserve jar, cover, and let stand ten minutes; place jar on trivet in saucepan surrounded with cold water. Heat gradually on back of range; keep water just simmering for one hour. Strain, add salt, and serve in hot cup.

div.head: Beef Essence
div.p: Wipe one half pound round steak; remove fat; chop very fine; place in fruit jar; cover, place jar on trivet, surround with cold water, and keep water just bubbling for one and a half hours. Strain, press meat to extract all juice, season, serve in hot cup.

div.head: Frozen Beef Tea
div.p: Prepare Beef Tea, pour into glass, surrounded with ice and salt, and freeze, turning glass often, and scraping the frozen part into the liquid.

div.head: Scraped Beef Balls
div.p: Prepare scraped beef according to rule. Season; shape in round balls about the size of marbles; cook in hissing hot frying pan; keep pan constantly in motion, and cook balls two minutes. Serve on small strips of toasted bread; garnish with parsley.

div.head: Mutton Broth
div.p: Wipe two pounds neck of mutton; remove all fat and cut off skin; cut meat in small pieces. Put meat and bones in kettle; add four cups cold water, and simmer gently several hours; add salt to taste. Strain, let stand over night to cool; in the morning remove fat, reheat, and serve with two tablespoons cooked rice in broth.

div.head: Chicken Broth
div.p: Cut up a three-pound fowl; remove skin and all fat. Put in soup kettle; add ten cups cold water, and simmer until meat falls from bones. Strain; let stand over night to cool; remove fat; reheat, season with salt, and serve with Boiled Rice or Croûtons.

div.head: Clam Broth
div.p: Wash one dozen clams, put in kettle, cover, and cook until shells open. Strain clam liquor through cheese cloth and serve very hot.

div.head: Rennet Custard

list.item:
4 cups milk
1 tablespoon liquid rennet
1 tablespoon brandy
few grains salt
4 tablespoons sugar

div.p: Mix sugar, brandy and salt. Heat milk until lukewarm; add rennet and other ingredients; pour into serving dish and let stand until a firm curd is formed, then chill. Serve with cream and sugar.

div.head: Calf’s Foot Jelly

list.item:
1 calf’s foot
4 cups cold water
½ cup sherry
½ cup lemon juice
½ cup sugar
3 egg whites

div.p: Cook the calf’s foot in cold water, slowly, for four hours. Skim often while cooking. Strain; let stand over night. Remove fat; add whites of eggs slightly beaten, and bring slowly to the boiling point, stirring all of the time; boil one minute, strain through cheese cloth, add remaining ingredients, and pour into molds. Chill and serve.

div.head: Strawberry Whip

list.item:
2 egg whites
½ cup powdered sugar
1 cup strawberries
1 tablespoon lemon juice

div.p: Hull and wash the strawberries, add sugar and lemon juice. Beat the whites of eggs until stiff, add other ingredients, and serve ice-cold in frappé glasses.

div.head: Arrowroot Blanc Mange

list.item:
2 tablespoons arrowroot
few grains of salt
2 tablespoons sugar
1⅓ cups milk
flavoring

div.p: Mix arrowroot, salt and sugar; add milk, a little at a time, until the mixture is smooth, then add the remainder, and cook in double boiler one half hour, stirring all the time. Add flavoring, pour into molds, and serve with Soft Custard or cream.

div.head: Stewed Prunes
div.p: Wash prunes; soak over night in water to cover; cook slowly, in same water, until tender. A small amount of sugar and lemon juice may be added if desired.

div.head: Stewed Figs
div.p: Wash figs; cut in pieces; for each cup of figs add one quarter cup cold water, simmer one hour; add sugar and lemon juice if allowed.

div.head: Oatmeal Wafers

list.item:
1 cup flour
½ cup fine oatmeal
⅓ cup rolled oats
4 tablespoons sugar
2 tablespoons butter
½ teaspoon salt
⅓ cup hot milk
1 teaspoon lemon juice

div.p: Mix butter and milk; when cool, add remaining ingredients. Roll very thin, shape in squares, and bake in a slow oven.

div.head: Hoe Cake

list.item:
1 cup white corn meal
¼ teaspoon salt
¼ cup boiling water
milk
1 teaspoon baking powder

div.p: Mix salt and corn meal, add boiling water, let stand ten minutes. Add baking powder and sufficient milk to make a stiff batter. Grease a griddle; when hot, drop the mixture by spoonfuls on to it. When brown put a piece of butter on top of each cake and turn.

div.head: Corn Pone

list.item:
2 cups coarse corn meal
water to make a soft dough
1 teaspoon salt
